  <Tab value="python" label="Python">
    <WrapCode>
      ```python file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk-python/examples/rag_turbovec.py title="rag_turbovec.py" lineNumbers
      """Python port of packages/sdk/examples/rag/rag-turbovec.ts.

      Retrieval over documents kept in your own store. The SDK holds only the
      vectors, in a TurboVec index inside the worker; the documents stay in this dict
      (or any database you choose) and result ids map back to them.

      `vector_index` is a generated request-reply method covering every index
      operation. Where the JS SDK hands back an index object with `add`/`search`/
      `write`/`dispose` methods, `create` here returns an `indexId` that every later
      operation carries. `search` is batched: it takes `queries` and returns one
      result list per query. `VectorIndexStorage` is a plain enum, so pass its
      `.value` â€” the wire contract takes the string.

      RUN: python examples/rag_turbovec.py [query]
      """

      from __future__ import annotations

      import asyncio
      import sys

      from tetherto.qvac_sdk import (
          Client,
          EmbedRequest,
          VectorIndexRequest,
          VectorIndexStorage,
          embed,
          load_model,
          unload_model,
          vector_index,
      )
      from tetherto.qvac_sdk.models import GTE_LARGE_FP16


      def print_progress(p) -> None:
          """Print model download progress; pass as `on_progress=` to `load_model`."""
          line = (
              f"â–¸ Downloading {p.percentage:.0f}% "
              f"({p.downloaded / 1e6:.1f}/{p.total / 1e6:.1f} MB)"
          )
          print(line, end="\r" if sys.stderr.isatty() else "\n", file=sys.stderr)
          if p.percentage >= 100:
              print(file=sys.stderr)


      async def embed_text(t, model_id, text):
          """Embed one string or a list of strings; returns the vector(s)."""
          response = await embed(
              t,
              EmbedRequest.model_validate(
                  {"type": "embed", "modelId": model_id, "text": text}
              ),
          )
          if not response.success:
              raise RuntimeError(response.error)
          return response.embedding


      async def main() -> int:
          async with Client() as client:
              t = client.transport
              try:
                  query = (
                      sys.argv[1]
                      if len(sys.argv) > 1
                      else "Which moon has methane rain and lakes?"
                  )
                  print(f'â–¸ Query: "{query}"')

                  # Ids are numeric by contract, so keep your own id as the key and
                  # let the index hold only the numeric handle plus the vector.
                  documents = {
                      "1": "Saturn moon Titan has lakes, clouds, and rain made of liquid methane.",
                      "2": "Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity using photovoltaic cells.",
                      "3": "Honeybees communicate the location of flowers through a waggle dance.",
                      "4": "The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth.",
                  }

                  model_id = await load_model(
                      t, model_src=GTE_LARGE_FP16, on_progress=print_progress
                  )

                  print("â–¸ Embedding documents...")
                  vectors = await embed_text(t, model_id, list(documents.values()))

                  print("â–¸ Building the vector index...")
                  created = await vector_index(
                      t,
                      VectorIndexRequest.model_validate(
                          {
                              "type": "vectorIndex",
                              "operation": "create",
                              "dim": len(vectors[0]),
                              "storage": VectorIndexStorage.turbovec_q4.value,
                          }
                      ),
                  )
                  index_id = created.root.index_id
                  added = await vector_index(
                      t,
                      VectorIndexRequest.model_validate(
                          {
                              "type": "vectorIndex",
                              "operation": "add",
                              "indexId": index_id,
                              "ids": list(documents.keys()),
                              "vectors": vectors,
                          }
                      ),
                  )
                  print(
                      f"â–¸ Indexed {added.root.length} vectors of dimension {created.root.dim}"
                  )

                  print("â–¸ Searching...")
                  query_vector = await embed_text(t, model_id, query)
                  found = await vector_index(
                      t,
                      VectorIndexRequest.model_validate(
                          {
                              "type": "vectorIndex",
                              "operation": "search",
                              "indexId": index_id,
                              "queries": [query_vector],
                              "k": 2,
                          }
                      ),
                  )
                  hits = found.root.results[0]
                  print("â–¸ Top matches:")
                  for hit in hits:
                      print(f"  score={hit.score:.4f} id={hit.id}: {documents[hit.id]}")

                  # Snapshots persist the vectors only. A relative path resolves under
                  # the QVAC data directory; pass an absolute path to store it elsewhere.
                  snapshot_path = "examples/rag_turbovec.qvi"
                  written = await vector_index(
                      t,
                      VectorIndexRequest.model_validate(
                          {
                              "type": "vectorIndex",
                              "operation": "write",
                              "indexId": index_id,
                              "path": snapshot_path,
                          }
                      ),
                  )
                  await vector_index(
                      t,
                      VectorIndexRequest.model_validate(
                          {
                              "type": "vectorIndex",
                              "operation": "dispose",
                              "indexId": index_id,
                          }
                      ),
                  )
                  print(f"â–¸ Snapshot written to {written.root.path}")

                  reloaded = await vector_index(
                      t,
                      VectorIndexRequest.model_validate(
                          {
                              "type": "vectorIndex",
                              "operation": "load",
                              "path": snapshot_path,
                          }
                      ),
                  )
                  reloaded_id = reloaded.root.index_id
                  reloaded_found = await vector_index(
                      t,
                      VectorIndexRequest.model_validate(
                          {
                              "type": "vectorIndex",
                              "operation": "search",
                              "indexId": reloaded_id,
                              "queries": [query_vector],
                              "k": 1,
                          }
                      ),
                  )
                  reloaded_hits = reloaded_found.root.results[0]
                  reloaded_best = reloaded_hits[0] if reloaded_hits else None
                  await vector_index(
                      t,
                      VectorIndexRequest.model_validate(
                          {
                              "type": "vectorIndex",
                              "operation": "dispose",
                              "indexId": reloaded_id,
                          }
                      ),
                  )
                  best = hits[0] if hits else None
                  if reloaded_best is None or best is None or reloaded_best.id != best.id:
                      raise RuntimeError(
                          f"Reloaded index returned id="
                          f"{reloaded_best.id if reloaded_best else None} but the "
                          f"original returned id={best.id if best else None}"
                      )
                  print(f"â–¸ Reloaded index agrees: best match id={reloaded_best.id}")

                  await unload_model(t, model_id)
              except Exception as error:
                  print(f"âœ– {error}", file=sys.stderr)
                  return 1
          return 0


      if __name__ == "__main__":
          sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))
      ```
    </WrapCode>
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="info">
  TurboVec quantises vectors (`VectorIndexStorage.TURBOVEC_Q4` by default, `TURBOVEC_Q2` for half the memory) and needs a dimension divisible by 8 and no greater than 1024. `GTE_LARGE_FP16` produces 1024-dimensional vectors and fits. Search uses dot products, so L2-normalise vectors when you need cosine similarity. The index lives in the SDK worker; after a worker restart, reopen it from the snapshot.
</Callout>

### External vector DB

#### MongoDB

This example needs two things the SDK does not provide: a MongoDB driver, and a deployment with Atlas Vector Search. Install the driver for the language you are using â€” `npm i "mongodb@^7.5.0"` for JavaScript and TypeScript, or `pip install "pymongo>=4.13"` for Python. Those are the versions these docs are tested against.

One way to get a deployment is the Atlas local container:

```bash
docker run -p 27017:27017 --name atlas-local mongodb/mongodb-atlas-local
```

The script connects to `mongodb://localhost:27017/?directConnection=true`; edit that connection string if your deployment lives elsewhere.

The following script stores each document in MongoDB alongside its vector, builds a vector search index over it, and retrieves matches with a `$vectorSearch` aggregation that [pre-filters](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage/#pre-filter-search-data) by category:

<Tabs>
  <Tab value="js" label="JavaScript" default>
    <WrapCode>
      ```js file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk/dist/examples/rag/rag-mongodb.js title="rag-mongodb.js" lineNumbers
      import { embed, loadModel, unloadModel, GTE_LARGE_FP16 } from '@qvac/sdk';
      import { MongoClient } from 'mongodb';
      const INDEX_NAME = 'documents_vector_index';
      const MONGODB_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS = `
      â–¸ This example needs a MongoDB deployment with Atlas Vector Search.

      One way to get one is to run it in Docker:

         docker run -p 27017:27017 --name atlas-local mongodb/mongodb-atlas-local

      For more details, visit: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-deploy-docker/
      `;
      async function initializeMongoClient() {
          // Replace with your own deployment's connection string if it is not the Docker one
          // https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string/
          const client = new MongoClient('mongodb://localhost:27017/?directConnection=true');
          try {
              await client.connect();
              await client.db('admin').command({ ping: 1 });
              console.log('â–¸ Connected to MongoDB server');
              return client;
          }
          catch {
              console.error('âœ– Failed to connect to MongoDB server');
              console.error('â–¸ Please ensure the server is running on localhost:27017');
              console.error(MONGODB_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS);
              process.exit(1);
          }
      }
      function wait(ms) {
          return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
      }
      try {
          // Get query and category from command line or use defaults
          const query = process.argv[2] || 'machine learning algorithms';
          const category = process.argv[3] || 'ai';
          console.log(`â–¸ Query: "${query}" (category: "${category}")`);
          const client = await initializeMongoClient();
          const collection = client.db('qvac').collection('documents');
          const modelId = await loadModel({
              modelSrc: GTE_LARGE_FP16,
              onProgress: (p) => {
                  const mb = (n) => (n / 1e6).toFixed(1);
                  const line = `â–¸ Downloading ${p.percentage.toFixed(0)}% (${mb(p.downloaded)}/${mb(p.total)} MB)`;
                  process.stderr.write(process.stderr.isTTY ? `\r${line}` : `${line}\n`);
                  if (p.percentage >= 100)
                      process.stderr.write('\n');
              }
          });
          // Sample corpus, each document tagged with a category to filter on
          const samples = [
              {
                  id: 1,
                  category: 'ai',
                  text: 'Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on algorithms that can learn and make predictions from data without being explicitly programmed for every task.'

              }

                      {
                          type: 'filter',
                          path: 'category'
                      }
                  ]
              }
          });
          // Index builds are asynchronous; querying too early returns no matches
          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 60; attempt++) {
              const [index] = (await collection.listSearchIndexes(INDEX_NAME).toArray());
              if (index?.queryable)
                  break;
              if (attempt === 59)
                  throw new Error(`Index ${INDEX_NAME} did not become queryable`);
              await wait(1000);
          }
          console.log('â–¸ Searching for similar documents...');
          const { embedding: queryEmbedding } = await embed({ modelId, text: query });
          const results = await collection
              .aggregate([
              {
                  $vectorSearch: {

                      path: 'embedding',
                      queryVector: queryEmbedding,
                      filter: { category: { $eq: category } },
                      numCandidates: 100,
                      limit: 3
                  }
              },
              {
                  $project: {
                      _id: 0,
                      id: 1,
                      category: 1,
                      text: 1,
                      score: { $meta: 'vectorSearchScore' }
                  }
              }
          ])
              .toArray();
          console.log('â–¸ Top 3 most similar documents:');
          results.forEach((result, index) => {
              console.log(`${index + 1}. (Score: ${result.score.toFixed(4)}, Category: ${result.category})`);
              console.log(`   ${result.text}`);
              console.log();
          });
          await unloadModel({ modelId });
          await client.close();
      }
      catch (error) {
      ```

    <WrapCode>
      ```python file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk-python/examples/rag_mongodb.py title="rag_mongodb.py" lineNumbers
      """Python port of packages/sdk/examples/rag/rag-mongodb.ts.

      Store each document in MongoDB alongside its vector, build a vector search
      index over it, and retrieve matches with a `$vectorSearch` aggregation that
      pre-filters by category.

      Needs the MongoDB driver (`pip install pymongo`) and a deployment with Atlas
      Vector Search. QVAC only produces the vectors through `embed`; the storage,
      indexing and search all belong to MongoDB.

      The driver's asyncio API mirrors the JS one closely: `AsyncMongoClient`, and
      every collection call awaited. Two differences worth knowing: `drop()` is
      idempotent (the driver allows "ns not found"), so dropping a collection that
      was never created needs no guard, and the index-build poll sleeps with
      `asyncio.sleep` instead of a hand-rolled promise timer.

      RUN: python examples/rag_mongodb.py [query] [category]
      """

      from __future__ import annotations

      import asyncio
      import sys

      from tetherto.qvac_sdk import Client, EmbedRequest, embed, load_model, unload_model
      from tetherto.qvac_sdk.models import GTE_LARGE_FP16

      INDEX_NAME = "documents_vector_index"

      MONGODB_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS = """
      â–¸ This example needs a MongoDB deployment with Atlas Vector Search.

      One way to get one is to run it in Docker:

         docker run -p 27017:27017 --name atlas-local mongodb/mongodb-atlas-local

      For more details, visit: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-deploy-docker/
      """


      def print_progress(p) -> None:
          """Print model download progress; pass as `on_progress=` to `load_model`."""
          line = (
              f"â–¸ Downloading {p.percentage:.0f}% "
              f"({p.downloaded / 1e6:.1f}/{p.total / 1e6:.1f} MB)"
          )
          print(line, end="\r" if sys.stderr.isatty() else "\n", file=sys.stderr)
          if p.percentage >= 100:
              print(file=sys.stderr)


      async def embed_text(t, model_id, text):
          """Embed one string or a list of strings; returns the vector(s)."""
          response = await embed(
              t,
              EmbedRequest.model_validate(
                  {"type": "embed", "modelId": model_id, "text": text}
              ),
          )
          if not response.success:
              raise RuntimeError(response.error)
          return response.embedding


      async def main() -> int:
          try:
              from pymongo import AsyncMongoClient
              from pymongo.errors import PyMongoError
              from pymongo.operations import SearchIndexModel
          except ImportError:
              print("âœ– This example needs pymongo: pip install pymongo", file=sys.stderr)
              return 1

          # Get query and category from command line or use defaults
          query = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "machine learning algorithms"
          category = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "ai"
          print(f'â–¸ Query: "{query}" (category: "{category}")')

          # Replace with your own deployment's connection string if it is not the Docker one
          # https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string/
          mongo = AsyncMongoClient("mongodb://localhost:27017/?directConnection=true")
          try:
              await mongo.admin.command("ping")
              print("â–¸ Connected to MongoDB server")
          except PyMongoError:
              print("âœ– Failed to connect to MongoDB server", file=sys.stderr)
              print(
                  "â–¸ Please ensure the server is running on localhost:27017", file=sys.stderr
              )
              print(MONGODB_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS, file=sys.stderr)
              await mongo.close()
              return 1

          collection = mongo["qvac"]["documents"]

          try:
              async with Client() as client:
                  t = client.transport
                  model_id = await load_model(
                      t, model_src=GTE_LARGE_FP16, on_progress=print_progress
                  )

                  # Sample corpus, each document tagged with a category to filter on
                  samples = [
                      {
                          "id": 1,
                          "category": "ai",
                          "text": "Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on algorithms that can learn and make predictions from data without being explicitly programmed for every task.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 2,
                          "category": "ai",
                          "text": "Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers to process and learn from complex data patterns, enabling breakthroughs in image recognition and natural language processing.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 3,
                          "category": "ai",
                          "text": "Natural language processing combines computational linguistics with machine learning to help computers understand, interpret, and generate human language in a meaningful way.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 4,
                          "category": "ai",
                          "text": "Computer vision enables machines to interpret and understand visual information from the world, using techniques like image classification, object detection, and facial recognition.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 5,
                          "category": "computing",
                          "text": "Quantum computing leverages quantum mechanical phenomena to process information in fundamentally different ways than classical computers, potentially solving certain problems exponentially faster.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 6,
                          "category": "security",
                          "text": "Blockchain technology creates decentralized, immutable ledgers that enable secure peer-to-peer transactions without requiring a central authority or intermediary.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 7,
                          "category": "computing",
                          "text": "Cloud computing delivers computing services over the internet, allowing users to access resources like storage, processing power, and applications on-demand from anywhere.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 8,
                          "category": "security",
                          "text": "Cybersecurity protects digital systems, networks, and data from malicious attacks, unauthorized access, and various forms of cyber threats through multiple layers of defense.",
                      },
                  ]

                  # (Re)create the collection. The driver allows "ns not found", so
                  # this is a no-op the first time round.
                  await collection.drop()

                  # Embed and store documents
                  print("â–¸ Embedding documents...")
                  documents = []
                  for sample in samples:
                      embedding = await embed_text(t, model_id, sample["text"])
                      documents.append(
                          {
                              "id": sample["id"],
                              "category": sample["category"],
                              "text": sample["text"],
                              "embedding": embedding,
                          }
                      )

                  await collection.insert_many(documents)

                  # numDimensions is fixed at index creation and must match the model:
                  # GTE Large is 1024
                  print("â–¸ Creating vector search index...")
                  await collection.create_search_index(
                      SearchIndexModel(
                          name=INDEX_NAME,
                          type="vectorSearch",
                          definition={
                              "fields": [
                                  {
                                      "type": "vector",
                                      "path": "embedding",
                                      "numDimensions": 1024,
                                      "similarity": "cosine",
                                  },
                                  # A field must be indexed as a filter to be usable
                                  # in a $vectorSearch filter
                                  {"type": "filter", "path": "category"},
                              ]
                          },
                      )
                  )

                  # Index builds are asynchronous; querying too early returns no matches
                  for attempt in range(60):
                      cursor = await collection.list_search_indexes(INDEX_NAME)
                      indexes = await cursor.to_list()
                      if indexes and indexes[0].get("queryable"):
                          break
                      if attempt == 59:
                          raise RuntimeError(f"Index {INDEX_NAME} did not become queryable")
                      await asyncio.sleep(1)

                  print("â–¸ Searching for similar documents...")
                  query_vector = await embed_text(t, model_id, query)

                  cursor = await collection.aggregate(
                      [
                          {
                              "$vectorSearch": {
                                  "index": INDEX_NAME,
                                  "path": "embedding",
                                  "queryVector": query_vector,
                                  "filter": {"category": {"$eq": category}},
                                  "numCandidates": 100,
                                  "limit": 3,
                              }
                          },
                          {
                              "$project": {
                                  "_id": 0,
                                  "id": 1,
                                  "category": 1,
                                  "text": 1,
                                  "score": {"$meta": "vectorSearchScore"},
                              }
                          },
                      ]
                  )
                  results = await cursor.to_list()

                  print("â–¸ Top 3 most similar documents:")
                  for index, result in enumerate(results, start=1):
                      print(
                          f"{index}. (Score: {result['score']:.4f}, "
                          f"Category: {result['category']})"
                      )
                      print(f"   {result['text']}")
                      print()

                  await unload_model(t, model_id)
          except Exception as error:
              print(f"âœ– {error}", file=sys.stderr)
              return 1
          finally:
              await mongo.close()
          return 0


      if __name__ == "__main__":
          sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))
      ```

#### SQLite

This example needs the vector extension for SQLite, which arrives differently per language. JavaScript and TypeScript use a SQLite WASM build that has the extension compiled in; Python uses the standard library's `sqlite3` module and loads the extension from a prebuilt binary. Install the one for the language you are using:

```bash
# JavaScript and TypeScript
npm i "@sqliteai/sqlite-wasm@3.50.4-sync.0.8.30-vector.0.9.23"

# Python
pip install "sqliteai-vector>=1.1"
```

Those are the versions these docs are tested against. Loading an extension also needs a Python configured with `--enable-loadable-sqlite-extensions`. Most distribution and python.org builds are; `pyenv`'s default build is not, and no package you install changes that â€” pass `-p` to `virtualenv` (or `--python` to `uv venv`) to base the environment on an interpreter that qualifies. The example checks before it starts and tells you if yours does not. The database is in-memory, so there is nothing else to set up.

The following script shows the same workflow using `embed()` plus a SQLite vector index:

<Tabs>
  <Tab value="js" label="JavaScript" default>
    <WrapCode>
      ```js file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk/dist/examples/rag/rag-sqlite.js title="rag-sqlite.js" lineNumbers
      import { embed, loadModel, unloadModel, GTE_LARGE_FP16 } from '@qvac/sdk';
      import sqlite3InitModule from '@sqliteai/sqlite-wasm';
      try {
          // Get query from command line or use default
          const query = process.argv[2] || 'machine learning algorithms';
          console.log(`â–¸ Query: "${query}"`);
          // Initialize SQLite with vector extension
          const sqlite3 = await sqlite3InitModule();
          const db = new sqlite3.oo1.DB(':memory:', 'c');
          const modelId = await loadModel({
              modelSrc: GTE_LARGE_FP16,
              onProgress: (p) => {
                  const mb = (n) => (n / 1e6).toFixed(1);
                  const line = `â–¸ Downloading ${p.percentage.toFixed(0)}% (${mb(p.downloaded)}/${mb(p.total)} MB)`;
                  process.stderr.write(process.stderr.isTTY ? `\r${line}` : `${line}\n`);
                  if (p.percentage >= 100)
                      process.stderr.write('\n');
              }
          });
          const samples = [
              {
                  id: 1,
                  text: 'Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on algorithms that can learn and make predictions from data without being explicitly programmed for every task.'
              },
              {
                  id: 2,
                  text: 'Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers to process and learn from complex data patterns, enabling breakthroughs in image recognition and natural language processing.'
              },
              {
                  id: 3,
                  text: 'Natural language processing combines computational linguistics with machine learning to help computers understand, interpret, and generate human language in a meaningful way.'
              },
              {
                  id: 4,
                  text: 'Computer vision enables machines to interpret and understand visual information from the world, using techniques like image classification, object detection, and facial recognition.'
              },
              {
                  id: 5,
                  text: 'Quantum computing leverages quantum mechanical phenomena to process information in fundamentally different ways than classical computers, potentially solving certain problems exponentially faster.'
              },
              {
                  id: 6,
                  text: 'Blockchain technology creates decentralized, immutable ledgers that enable secure peer-to-peer transactions without requiring a central authority or intermediary.'
              },
              {
                  id: 7,
                  text: 'Cloud computing delivers computing services over the internet, allowing users to access resources like storage, processing power, and applications on-demand from anywhere.'
              },
              {
                  id: 8,
                  text: 'Cybersecurity protects digital systems, networks, and data from malicious attacks, unauthorized access, and various forms of cyber threats through multiple layers of defense.'
              }
          ];
          // Create table for documents with vector storage
          db.exec(`
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
          id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
          text TEXT NOT NULL,
          embedding BLOB NOT NULL
        )
      `);
          console.log('â–¸ Embedding documents...');
          for (const sample of samples) {
              const { embedding } = await embed({ modelId, text: sample.text });
              db.exec({
                  sql: 'INSERT INTO documents VALUES (?, ?, vector_as_f32(?))',
                  bind: [sample.id, sample.text, JSON.stringify(embedding)]
              });
          }
          // Initialize and optimize vector index
          db.exec(`SELECT vector_init('documents', 'embedding', 'type=FLOAT32,dimension=1024')`);
          // Quantize vectors
          db.exec(`SELECT vector_quantize('documents', 'embedding')`);
          // [Optional] Preload quantized vectors in memory for optimal performance
          db.exec(`SELECT vector_quantize_preload('documents', 'embedding')`);
          // Search for similar documents
          console.log('â–¸ Searching for similar documents...');
          const { embedding: queryEmbedding } = await embed({ modelId, text: query });
          const results = [];
          // Perform vector search
          db.exec({
              sql: `
          SELECT d.id, d.text, v.distance 
          FROM documents d
          JOIN vector_quantize_scan('documents', 'embedding', vector_as_f32(?), 3) v
          ON d.id = v.rowid
        `,
              bind: [JSON.stringify(queryEmbedding)],
              rowMode: 'object',
              callback: (row) => {
                  const typedRow = row;
                  results.push(typedRow);
              }
          });
          console.log('\nâ–¸ Top 3 most similar documents:');
          results.forEach((result, index) => {
              console.log('='.repeat(50) + ' Top result:');
              console.log(`\n${index + 1}. [ID: ${result.id}] (Score: ${result.distance.toFixed(4)})`);
              console.log(`   ${result.text}`);
              console.log('='.repeat(100));
              console.log();
          });
          await unloadModel({ modelId });
          db.close();
      }
      catch (error) {
          console.error('âœ–', error);
          process.exit(1);
      }
      ```

      ```ts file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk/examples/rag/rag-sqlite.ts title="rag-sqlite.ts" lineNumbers
          onProgress: (p) => {
            const mb = (n: number) => (n / 1e6).toFixed(1)
            const line = `â–¸ Downloading ${p.percentage.toFixed(0)}% (${mb(p.downloaded)}/${mb(p.total)} MB)`
            process.stderr.write(process.stderr.isTTY ? `\r${line}` : `${line}\n`)
            if (p.percentage >= 100) process.stderr.write('\n')
          }
        })

        const samples = [
          {
            id: 1,
            text: 'Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on algorithms that can learn and make predictions from data without being explicitly programmed for every task.'
          },
          {
            id: 2,
            text: 'Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers to process and learn from complex data patterns, enabling breakthroughs in image recognition and natural language processing.'
          },
          {
            id: 3,
            text: 'Natural language processing combines computational linguistics with machine learning to help computers understand, interpret, and generate human language in a meaningful way.'
          },
          {
            id: 4,
            text: 'Computer vision enables machines to interpret and understand visual information from the world, using techniques like image classification, object detection, and facial recognition.'
          },
          {
            id: 5,
            text: 'Quantum computing leverages quantum mechanical phenomena to process information in fundamentally different ways than classical computers, potentially solving certain problems exponentially faster.'
          },
          {
            id: 6,
            text: 'Blockchain technology creates decentralized, immutable ledgers that enable secure peer-to-peer transactions without requiring a central authority or intermediary.'
          },
          {
            id: 7,
            text: 'Cloud computing delivers computing services over the internet, allowing users to access resources like storage, processing power, and applications on-demand from anywhere.'
          },
          {
            id: 8,
            text: 'Cybersecurity protects digital systems, networks, and data from malicious attacks, unauthorized access, and various forms of cyber threats through multiple layers of defense.'
          }
        ]

        // Create table for documents with vector storage
        db.exec(`
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
          id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
          text TEXT NOT NULL,
          embedding BLOB NOT NULL
        )
      `)

        console.log('â–¸ Embedding documents...')
        for (const sample of samples) {
          const { embedding } = await embed({ modelId, text: sample.text })
          db.exec({
            sql: 'INSERT INTO documents VALUES (?, ?, vector_as_f32(?))',
            bind: [sample.id, sample.text, JSON.stringify(embedding)]
          })
        }

        // Initialize and optimize vector index
        db.exec(`SELECT vector_init('documents', 'embedding', 'type=FLOAT32,dimension=1024')`)

        // Quantize vectors
        db.exec(`SELECT vector_quantize('documents', 'embedding')`)

        // [Optional] Preload quantized vectors in memory for optimal performance
        db.exec(`SELECT vector_quantize_preload('documents', 'embedding')`)

        // Search for similar documents
        console.log('â–¸ Searching for similar documents...')
        const { embedding: queryEmbedding } = await embed({ modelId, text: query })

        const results: Array<{
          id: number
          text: string
          distance: number
        }> = []

        // Perform vector search
        db.exec({
          sql: `
          SELECT d.id, d.text, v.distance 
          FROM documents d
          JOIN vector_quantize_scan('documents', 'embedding', vector_as_f32(?), 3) v
          ON d.id = v.rowid
        `,
          bind: [JSON.stringify(queryEmbedding)],
          rowMode: 'object',
          callback: (row: unknown) => {
            const typedRow = row as { id: number; text: string; distance: number }
            results.push(typedRow)
          }
        })

        console.log('\nâ–¸ Top 3 most similar documents:')
        results.forEach((result, index) => {
          console.log('='.repeat(50) + ' Top result:')
          console.log(`\n${index + 1}. [ID: ${result.id}] (Score: ${result.distance.toFixed(4)})`)
          console.log(`   ${result.text}`)
          console.log('='.repeat(100))
          console.log()
        })

        await unloadModel({ modelId })
        db.close()
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('âœ–', error)
        process.exit(1)
      }
      ```

  </Tab>

  <Tab value="python" label="Python">
    <WrapCode>
      ```python file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk-python/examples/rag_sqlite.py title="rag_sqlite.py" lineNumbers
      """Python port of packages/sdk/examples/rag/rag-sqlite.ts.

      Keep each document in SQLite alongside its vector and retrieve matches with
      the SQLite-Vector extension's quantized scan. QVAC only produces the vectors
      through `embed`; the storage, quantization and search all happen in SQL.

      The extension and its SQL are the same ones the TypeScript example uses, but
      they arrive differently. There the npm `@sqliteai/sqlite-wasm` build has the
      extension compiled in; here the stdlib `sqlite3` module loads a prebuilt
      binary, shipped by `pip install sqliteai-vector`. That needs an interpreter
      configured with `--enable-loadable-sqlite-extensions`, which pyenv's default
      build is not (`sqlite3.Connection.enable_load_extension` is absent when it is
      missing), so this example checks for it before trying.

      RUN: python examples/rag_sqlite.py [query]
      """

      from __future__ import annotations

      import asyncio
      import importlib.resources
      import json
      import sqlite3
      import sys

      from tetherto.qvac_sdk import Client, EmbedRequest, embed, load_model, unload_model
      from tetherto.qvac_sdk.models import GTE_LARGE_FP16


      def print_progress(p) -> None:
          """Print model download progress; pass as `on_progress=` to `load_model`."""
          line = (
              f"â–¸ Downloading {p.percentage:.0f}% "
              f"({p.downloaded / 1e6:.1f}/{p.total / 1e6:.1f} MB)"
          )
          print(line, end="\r" if sys.stderr.isatty() else "\n", file=sys.stderr)
          if p.percentage >= 100:
              print(file=sys.stderr)


      async def embed_text(t, model_id, text):
          """Embed one string or a list of strings; returns the vector(s)."""
          response = await embed(
              t,
              EmbedRequest.model_validate(
                  {"type": "embed", "modelId": model_id, "text": text}
              ),
          )
          if not response.success:
              raise RuntimeError(response.error)
          return response.embedding


      async def main() -> int:
          # Get query from command line or use default
          query = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "machine learning algorithms"
          print(f'â–¸ Query: "{query}"')

          # Initialize SQLite with vector extension
          db = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
          if not hasattr(db, "enable_load_extension"):
              print(
                  "âœ– This Python cannot load SQLite extensions, so the vector "
                  "extension is unavailable",
                  file=sys.stderr,
              )
              print(
                  "â–¸ Nothing is missing from your environment: the interpreter itself "
                  "must be built with --enable-loadable-sqlite-extensions. Most "
                  "distribution and python.org builds are; pyenv's default build is not",
                  file=sys.stderr,
              )
              return 1

          try:
              extension = importlib.resources.files("sqlite_vector.binaries") / "vector"
          except ModuleNotFoundError:
              print(
                  "âœ– This example needs the SQLite vector extension: "
                  "pip install sqliteai-vector",
                  file=sys.stderr,
              )
              return 1

          db.enable_load_extension(True)
          db.load_extension(str(extension))
          db.enable_load_extension(False)

          try:
              async with Client() as client:
                  t = client.transport
                  model_id = await load_model(
                      t, model_src=GTE_LARGE_FP16, on_progress=print_progress
                  )

                  samples = [
                      {
                          "id": 1,
                          "text": "Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on algorithms that can learn and make predictions from data without being explicitly programmed for every task.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 2,
                          "text": "Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers to process and learn from complex data patterns, enabling breakthroughs in image recognition and natural language processing.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 3,
                          "text": "Natural language processing combines computational linguistics with machine learning to help computers understand, interpret, and generate human language in a meaningful way.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 4,
                          "text": "Computer vision enables machines to interpret and understand visual information from the world, using techniques like image classification, object detection, and facial recognition.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 5,
                          "text": "Quantum computing leverages quantum mechanical phenomena to process information in fundamentally different ways than classical computers, potentially solving certain problems exponentially faster.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 6,
                          "text": "Blockchain technology creates decentralized, immutable ledgers that enable secure peer-to-peer transactions without requiring a central authority or intermediary.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 7,
                          "text": "Cloud computing delivers computing services over the internet, allowing users to access resources like storage, processing power, and applications on-demand from anywhere.",
                      },
                      {
                          "id": 8,
                          "text": "Cybersecurity protects digital systems, networks, and data from malicious attacks, unauthorized access, and various forms of cyber threats through multiple layers of defense.",
                      },
                  ]

                  # Create table for documents with vector storage
                  db.execute("""
                      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
                        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
                        text TEXT NOT NULL,
                        embedding BLOB NOT NULL
                      )
                  """)

                  print("â–¸ Embedding documents...")
                  for sample in samples:
                      embedding = await embed_text(t, model_id, sample["text"])
                      db.execute(
                          "INSERT INTO documents VALUES (?, ?, vector_as_f32(?))",
                          (sample["id"], sample["text"], json.dumps(embedding)),
                      )

                  # Initialize and optimize vector index
                  db.execute(
                      "SELECT vector_init('documents', 'embedding', ?)",
                      ("type=FLOAT32,dimension=1024",),
                  )

                  # Quantize vectors
                  db.execute("SELECT vector_quantize('documents', 'embedding')")

                  # [Optional] Preload quantized vectors in memory for optimal performance
                  db.execute("SELECT vector_quantize_preload('documents', 'embedding')")

                  # Search for similar documents
                  print("â–¸ Searching for similar documents...")
                  query_embedding = await embed_text(t, model_id, query)

                  # Perform vector search. The scan returns only rowid and distance,
                  # so the table is self-joined to read the text back.
                  results = db.execute(
                      """
                      SELECT d.id, d.text, v.distance
                      FROM documents d
                      JOIN vector_quantize_scan('documents', 'embedding', vector_as_f32(?), 3) v
                      ON d.id = v.rowid
                      """,
                      (json.dumps(query_embedding),),
                  ).fetchall()

                  print("\nâ–¸ Top 3 most similar documents:")
                  for index, (doc_id, text, distance) in enumerate(results, start=1):
                      print("=" * 50 + " Top result:")
                      print(f"\n{index}. [ID: {doc_id}] (Score: {distance:.4f})")
                      print(f"   {text}")
                      print("=" * 100)
                      print()

                  await unload_model(t, model_id)
          except Exception as error:
              print(f"âœ– {error}", file=sys.stderr)
              return 1
          finally:
              db.close()
          return 0


      if __name__ == "__main__":
          sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))
      ```
    </WrapCode>
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

# Reranking (/sdk/ai-capabilities/reranking)



## Overview

Reranking uses [`@qvac/embed-llamacpp`](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac/tree/main/packages/embed-llamacpp) with the Fabric LLM inference engine. Load a reranker (cross-encoder) model using `modelType: 'llamacpp-rerank'`. `modelConfig.device` defaults to `'gpu'`.

[`rerank()`](/sdk/reference/api#rerank) scores each document against a query. Pass a non-empty `query` and a non-empty array of `documents`.

`rerank()` returns one score per document, in the order the documents were given. Higher is more relevant. Scores are the model's raw classifier output (a logit for most rerankers), so they can be negative and are comparable only within one model. `rerank()` does not sort; sort the documents by score yourself, as the example below does.

## Functions

Use the following sequence of function calls:

1. [`loadModel()`](/sdk/reference/api#loadmodel)
2. [`rerank()`](/sdk/reference/api#rerank)
3. [`unloadModel()`](/sdk/reference/api#unloadmodel)

For how to use each function, see [SDK â€” API reference](/sdk/reference/api/).

## Models

Use a reranker GGUF, such as bge-reranker, jina-reranker or Qwen3-Reranker. The registry has no reranker constants yet, so pass a local GGUF path or a URL as `modelSrc` with explicit `modelType: 'llamacpp-rerank'`. For checkpoints split into multiple GGUF files, see [Sharded models](/sdk/models/sharded-models).

Rerankers and embedding models are not interchangeable: a reranker cannot be loaded for [`embed()`](/sdk/reference/api#embed), and an embedding model has no classifier head to score documents with.

The load-time `batch_size` sets the tokens per forward pass. Each document, paired with the query, must fit within it; the documents are packed into as few passes as fit. `threads`, `threads-batch`, `gpu_layers`, `flash_attn`, and `backend` control execution. The reranker fixes context size, pooling, and parallelism; these settings cannot be configured through the SDK.

## Cancellation and concurrency

The promise returned by [`rerank()`](/sdk/reference/api#rerank) exposes `requestId` before you await it. Pass that ID to [`cancel()`](/sdk/reference/api#cancel) to interrupt the request. Its promise rejects with `InferenceCancelledError`.

Each loaded model runs one rerank request at a time. Concurrent calls wait in a FIFO queue with up to 64 waiting requests per model. When the queue is full, additional calls reject with `RequestRejectedByPolicyError` without affecting active or queued requests. Cancelling a queued call by `requestId` rejects it with `InferenceCancelledError` before native work starts and leaves the active request running. See [Cancellation](/sdk/runtime/cancellation) for broad cancellation by model ID.

## Example

The following script loads a small reranker, or a GGUF path or URL passed as its first argument, scores four support articles against a question, and prints them from most to least relevant:

<Tabs>
  <Tab value="js" label="JavaScript" default>
    <WrapCode>
      ```js file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk/dist/examples/rerank.js title="rerank.js" lineNumbers
      import { loadModel, rerank, unloadModel, close } from '@qvac/sdk';
      // Any reranker (cross-encoder) GGUF, such as bge-reranker, jina-reranker or Qwen3-Reranker.
      const modelSrc = process.argv[2] ??
          'https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/models/resolve/499bc8821c6b12b4e53c5bffcb21ec206f212d81/jina-reranker-v1-tiny-en/ggml-model-f16.gguf';
      const query = 'How do I get a refund for a duplicate charge?';
      const documents = [
          'Refunds for duplicate or failed payments are issued within 5 business days.',
          'Our office is open Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm.',
          'To change your password, open Settings and choose Security.',
          'If you were charged twice, contact billing with both transaction IDs.'
      ];
      let modelId;
      try {
          console.error('â–¸ Loading reranker');
          modelId = await loadModel({ modelSrc, modelType: 'llamacpp-rerank' });
          // One score per document, in input order. Higher is more relevant.
          const scores = await rerank({ modelId, query, documents });
          const ranked = documents
              .map((document, index) => ({ score: scores[index], document }))
              .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);
          console.log(`Query: ${query}\n`);
          for (const { score, document } of ranked)
              console.log(`${score.toFixed(3)}  ${document}`);
      }
      catch (error) {
          console.error('âœ–', error);
          process.exitCode = 1;
      }
      finally {
          if (modelId)
              await unloadModel({ modelId });
          await close();
      }
      ```
    </WrapCode>
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="python" label="Python">
    <WrapCode>
      ```python file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk-python/examples/rerank.py title="rerank.py" lineNumbers
      """Python port of packages/sdk/examples/rerank.ts.

      Loads a small reranker, or a GGUF path or URL passed as the first argument,
      scores four support articles against a question, and prints them from most to
      least relevant.

      Python calls the generated `rerank` stub, so the request is a `RerankRequest`
      and the scores are read off the response. `Client` closes the SDK on exit,
      which the TypeScript example does with `close()`.

      RUN: python examples/rerank.py [path-or-url-to-reranker.gguf]
      """

      from __future__ import annotations

      import asyncio
      import sys

      from tetherto.qvac_sdk import (
          Client,
          RerankRequest,
          load_model,
          rerank,
          unload_model,
      )

      # Any reranker (cross-encoder) GGUF, such as bge-reranker, jina-reranker or
      # Qwen3-Reranker.
      DEFAULT_MODEL_SRC = (
          "https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/models/resolve/"
          "499bc8821c6b12b4e53c5bffcb21ec206f212d81/"
          "jina-reranker-v1-tiny-en/ggml-model-f16.gguf"
      )

      QUERY = "How do I get a refund for a duplicate charge?"
      DOCUMENTS = [
          "Refunds for duplicate or failed payments are issued within 5 business days.",
          "Our office is open Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm.",
          "To change your password, open Settings and choose Security.",
          "If you were charged twice, contact billing with both transaction IDs.",
      ]


      async def main() -> int:
          model_src = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else DEFAULT_MODEL_SRC

          async with Client() as client:
              t = client.transport
              model_id = None
              try:
                  print("â–¸ Loading reranker", file=sys.stderr)
                  model_id = await load_model(
                      t, model_src=model_src, model_type="llamacpp-rerank"
                  )
                  # One score per document, in input order. Higher is more relevant.
                  response = await rerank(
                      t,
                      RerankRequest.model_validate(
                          {
                              "type": "rerank",
                              "modelId": model_id,
                              "query": QUERY,
                              "documents": DOCUMENTS,
                          }
                      ),
                  )
                  ranked = sorted(
                      zip(response.scores, DOCUMENTS), key=lambda pair: pair[0], reverse=True
                  )
                  print(f"Query: {QUERY}\n")
                  for score, document in ranked:
                      print(f"{score:.3f}  {document}")
              except Exception as error:
                  print(f"âœ– {error}", file=sys.stderr)
                  return 1
              finally:
                  if model_id is not None:
                      await unload_model(t, model_id)
          return 0


      if __name__ == "__main__":
          sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))
      ```
    </WrapCode>
  </Tab>

# Text embeddings (/sdk/ai-capabilities/text-embeddings)



## Overview

Text embeddings uses [`qvac-fabric-llm.cpp`](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-fabric-llm.cpp) as inference engine. Load any supported model using `modelType: "embeddings"`. Then, provide text input as `text` where the value is either a single `string` or an array of strings.

`embed()` returns a single embedding vector (`number[]`) for single text input, or an array of embedding vectors (`number[][]`) for batch input.

`modelConfig.pooling` accepts `"none"`, `"mean"`, `"cls"`, or `"last"`. Omit it to use the model default. `"rank"` fails validation, including in `deviceDefaults` in [`qvac.config.*`](/sdk/configuration): it produces reranker scores, not embeddings, and `embed()` does not support reranker models; use [reranking](/sdk/ai-capabilities/reranking) for those.

## Functions

Use the following sequence of function calls:

1. [`loadModel()`](/sdk/reference/api#loadmodel)
2. [`embed()`](/sdk/reference/api#embed)
3. [`unloadModel()`](/sdk/reference/api#unloadmodel)

For how to use each function, see [SDK â€” API reference](/sdk/reference/api/).

## Models

You can load any [`llama.cpp`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp)-compatible embeddings model. Model file format: `*.gguf`.

* If the model is sharded across multiple files (a multi-file bundle), see [Sharded models](/sdk/models/sharded-models).
* For models available as constants, see [SDK â€” Models](/sdk#models).

## Example

The following script shows an example of embedding:

<Tabs>
  <Tab value="js" label="JavaScript" default>
    <WrapCode>
      ```js file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk/dist/examples/embed-p2p.js title="text-embeddings.js" lineNumbers
      import { embed, GTE_LARGE_FP16, loadModel, unloadModel } from '@qvac/sdk';
      function cosineSimilarity(vecA, vecB) {
          let dotProduct = 0;
          for (let i = 0; i < vecA.length; i++) {
              dotProduct += vecA[i] * vecB[i];
          }
          return dotProduct;
      }
      try {
          const modelId = await loadModel({
              modelSrc: GTE_LARGE_FP16,
              onProgress: (p) => {
                  const mb = (n) => (n / 1e6).toFixed(1);
                  const line = `â–¸ Downloading ${p.percentage.toFixed(0)}% (${mb(p.downloaded)}/${mb(p.total)} MB)`;
                  process.stderr.write(process.stderr.isTTY ? `\r${line}` : `${line}\n`);
                  if (p.percentage >= 100)
                      process.stderr.write('\n');
              },
              modelConfig: {
                  gpuLayers: 99,
                  device: 'gpu'
              }
          });
          console.log('\nâ–¸ Example 1: Single Text Embedding');
          console.log('='.repeat(50));
          const { embedding: singleEmbedding } = await embed({
              modelId,
              text: 'Hello, world!'
          });
          console.log("Input: 'Hello, world!'");
          console.log('Embedding dimensions:', singleEmbedding.length);
          console.log('First 10 values:', singleEmbedding.slice(0, 10));
          console.log('\nâ–¸ Example 2: Batch Text Embeddings');
          console.log('='.repeat(50));
          const texts = [
              'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog',
              'A fast auburn fox leaps over a sleepy canine',
              'Python is a programming language'
          ];
          const { embedding: batchEmbeddings } = await embed({ modelId, text: texts });
          console.log('Input: Array of', texts.length, 'texts');
          console.log('Output: Array of', batchEmbeddings.length, 'embeddings');
          const [emb1, emb2, emb3] = batchEmbeddings;
          if (!emb1 || !emb2 || !emb3) {
              throw new Error('Expected 3 embeddings');
          }
          console.log('Each embedding dimensions:', emb1.length);
          console.log('\nâ–¸ Similarity Analysis');
          console.log('='.repeat(50));
          const similarity1 = cosineSimilarity(emb1, emb2);
          const similarity2 = cosineSimilarity(emb1, emb3);
          console.log('Similarity between texts 1 and 2 (similar meaning):', similarity1.toFixed(4));
          console.log('Similarity between texts 1 and 3 (different topics):', similarity2.toFixed(4));
          console.log('\nâ–¸ Higher values indicate more similar meanings');
          await unloadModel({ modelId, clearStorage: false });
      }
      catch (error) {
          console.error('âœ–', error);
          process.exit(1);
      }
      ```
    </WrapCode>
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="ts" label="TypeScript">
    <WrapCode>
      ```ts file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk/examples/embed-p2p.ts title="text-embeddings.ts" lineNumbers
      import { embed, GTE_LARGE_FP16, loadModel, unloadModel } from '@qvac/sdk'

      function cosineSimilarity(vecA: number[], vecB: number[]) {
        let dotProduct = 0
        for (let i = 0; i < vecA.length; i++) {
          dotProduct += vecA[i]! * vecB[i]!
        }
        return dotProduct
      }

      try {
        const modelId = await loadModel({
          modelSrc: GTE_LARGE_FP16,
          onProgress: (p) => {
            const mb = (n: number) => (n / 1e6).toFixed(1)
            const line = `â–¸ Downloading ${p.percentage.toFixed(0)}% (${mb(p.downloaded)}/${mb(p.total)} MB)`
            process.stderr.write(process.stderr.isTTY ? `\r${line}` : `${line}\n`)
            if (p.percentage >= 100) process.stderr.write('\n')
          },
          modelConfig: {
            gpuLayers: 99,
            device: 'gpu'
          }
        })

        console.log('\nâ–¸ Example 1: Single Text Embedding')
        console.log('='.repeat(50))

        const { embedding: singleEmbedding } = await embed({
          modelId,
          text: 'Hello, world!'
        })

        console.log("Input: 'Hello, world!'")
        console.log('Embedding dimensions:', singleEmbedding.length)
        console.log('First 10 values:', singleEmbedding.slice(0, 10))

        console.log('\nâ–¸ Example 2: Batch Text Embeddings')
        console.log('='.repeat(50))

        const texts = [
          'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog',
          'A fast auburn fox leaps over a sleepy canine',
          'Python is a programming language'
        ]

        const { embedding: batchEmbeddings } = await embed({ modelId, text: texts })

        console.log('Input: Array of', texts.length, 'texts')
        console.log('Output: Array of', batchEmbeddings.length, 'embeddings')

        const [emb1, emb2, emb3] = batchEmbeddings

        if (!emb1 || !emb2 || !emb3) {
          throw new Error('Expected 3 embeddings')
        }

        console.log('Each embedding dimensions:', emb1.length)

        console.log('\nâ–¸ Similarity Analysis')
        console.log('='.repeat(50))

        const similarity1 = cosineSimilarity(emb1, emb2)
        const similarity2 = cosineSimilarity(emb1, emb3)

        console.log('Similarity between texts 1 and 2 (similar meaning):', similarity1.toFixed(4))
        console.log('Similarity between texts 1 and 3 (different topics):', similarity2.toFixed(4))
        console.log('\nâ–¸ Higher values indicate more similar meanings')

        await unloadModel({ modelId, clearStorage: false })
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('âœ–', error)
        process.exit(1)
      }
      ```

      ```python file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk-python/examples/embeddings.py title="embeddings.py" lineNumbers
      """Python port of packages/sdk/examples/embed-p2p.ts.

      Single + batch text embeddings and a cosine-similarity comparison.

      `embed` is a generated request-reply method: it takes a validated
      `EmbedRequest` and returns an `EmbedResponse` (there's no flat `embed(text=)`
      convenience wrapper yet). Request models are re-exported from the flat surface,
      so `from tetherto.qvac_sdk import EmbedRequest`.

      RUN: python examples/embeddings.py
      """

      from __future__ import annotations

      import asyncio
      import math
      import sys

      from tetherto.qvac_sdk import Client, EmbedRequest, embed, load_model, unload_model
      from tetherto.qvac_sdk.models import EMBEDDINGGEMMA_300M_Q4_0


      def print_progress(p) -> None:
          """Print model download progress; pass as `on_progress=` to `load_model`."""
          line = (
              f"â–¸ Downloading {p.percentage:.0f}% "
              f"({p.downloaded / 1e6:.1f}/{p.total / 1e6:.1f} MB)"
          )
          print(line, end="\r" if sys.stderr.isatty() else "\n", file=sys.stderr)
          if p.percentage >= 100:
              print(file=sys.stderr)


      def cosine_similarity(a, b) -> float:
          dot = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))
          na = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a))
          nb = math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b))
          return dot / (na * nb)


      async def embed_text(t, model_id, text):
          response = await embed(
              t,
              EmbedRequest.model_validate(
                  {"type": "embed", "modelId": model_id, "text": text}
              ),
          )
          if not response.success:
              raise RuntimeError(response.error)
          return response.embedding


      async def main() -> int:
          async with Client() as client:
              t = client.transport
              try:
                  model_id = await load_model(
                      t, model_src=EMBEDDINGGEMMA_300M_Q4_0, on_progress=print_progress
                  )

                  print("\nâ–¸ Example 1: Single Text Embedding")
                  print("=" * 50)
                  single = await embed_text(t, model_id, "Hello, world!")
                  print("Input: 'Hello, world!'")
                  print("Embedding dimensions:", len(single))
                  print("First 10 values:", single[:10])

                  print("\nâ–¸ Example 2: Batch Text Embeddings")
                  print("=" * 50)
                  texts = [
                      "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
                      "A fast auburn fox leaps over a sleepy canine",
                      "Python is a programming language",
                  ]
                  batch = await embed_text(t, model_id, texts)
                  print("Input: Array of", len(texts), "texts")
                  print("Output: Array of", len(batch), "embeddings")
                  emb1, emb2, emb3 = batch
                  print("Each embedding dimensions:", len(emb1))

                  print("\nâ–¸ Similarity Analysis")
                  print("=" * 50)
                  print(
                      "Similarity between texts 1 and 2 (similar meaning):",
                      f"{cosine_similarity(emb1, emb2):.4f}",
                  )
                  print(
                      "Similarity between texts 1 and 3 (different topics):",
                      f"{cosine_similarity(emb1, emb3):.4f}",
                  )
                  print("\nâ–¸ Higher values indicate more similar meanings")

                  await unload_model(t, model_id)
              except Exception as error:
                  print(f"âœ– {error}", file=sys.stderr)
                  return 1
          return 0


      if __name__ == "__main__":
          sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))
      ```

# Text generation (/sdk/ai-capabilities/text-generation)



## Overview

Text generation uses [`qvac-fabric-llm.cpp`](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-fabric-llm.cpp) as inference engine. Load any supported model using `modelType: "llm"`. Then, provide array `history` as input where each element is an object with properties:

* `role: string`; can be either `"user"` or `"assistant"`
* `content: string`

`role: "user"` indicates that `content` is a previous prompt.  `role: "assistant"` indicates that `content` is a previous inference (LLM output).

Output is generated based on the full sequence of messages provided in `history`.

## Functions

Use the following sequence of function calls:

1. [`loadModel()`](/sdk/reference/api#loadmodel)
2. [`completion()`](/sdk/reference/api#completion)
3. [`unloadModel()`](/sdk/reference/api#unloadmodel)

For how to use each function, see [SDK â€” API reference](/sdk/reference/api/).

## Models

You can load any [`llama.cpp`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp)-compatible text-generation/chat model. Model file format: `*.gguf`.

* If the model is sharded across multiple files (a multi-file bundle), see [Sharded models](/sdk/models/sharded-models).
* To adapt a model to domain-specific tasks, see [Fine-tuning](/sdk/ai-capabilities/fine-tuning).
* For models available as constants, see [SDK â€” Models](/sdk#models).

## Features

* Event stream: `completion()` exposes a single ordered `events` async iterable plus an aggregated `final` promise. Events are discriminated by `type` â€” `contentDelta`, `thinkingDelta`, `toolCall`, `toolError`, `completionStats`, `completionDone`, `rawDelta`. The terminal `completionDone` event carries a `stopReason` (e.g. `"eos"`, `"length"`, `"cancelled"`).
* Thinking content: models that emit `<think>` blocks surface them as dedicated `thinkingDelta` events (enable with `captureThinking: true`), so consumers don't have to parse tags from raw text.
* Tool calls: the model emits structured tool calls as `toolCall` events ordered alongside content and thinking in the same stream.
* Tool choice: `generationParams.tool_choice` takes `"auto"` (default), `"required"`, `"none"` or the name of a declared tool. On llama.cpp-backed models the sampler is constrained by the chat template's tool-call grammar, so `"required"` guarantees a call and a name restricts the call to that tool; a request that cannot honour the choice fails instead of answering in prose.
* Tool parameters: a tool's `parameters` is a JSON Schema object and is passed to the model as declared, including nested `properties`, `items`, nullable types (`["string", "null"]`) and `anyOf`. Zod `parameters` are converted with `z.toJSONSchema`, so nested Zod objects and arrays keep their structure.
* Tool errors: a tool-call region the model emitted that fails to parse or validate surfaces as a `toolError` event and in `final.toolErrors`, so an empty `toolCalls` can be told apart from a malformed call.
* Past tool calls in history: an `assistant` message carries the calls it made in `toolCalls` (`id`, `name`, `arguments`), and a `tool` message names the call it answers with `toolCallId` and `toolName`. llama.cpp-backed models render them with their own chat template instead of reading them as text in `content`.
* Parallel tool calls: one response may carry several tool calls on llama.cpp-backed models. `generationParams.parallel_tool_calls` defaults to `true`; set it to `false` to get at most one.
* MCP: plug MCP servers into `completion()` so the model can use external tools (e.g., web search) via the same tool-call mechanism.
* Raw output: with `emitRawDeltas: true`, every raw model token is also emitted as a `rawDelta` event in parallel to the structured events â€” useful for debugging or full-fidelity logging.
* KV cache: cache and reuse the model's key/value attention state to speed up follow-up turns in long conversations. The `kvCache` parameter sets the cache key â€” pass a string to manage a session manually, or `true` to let the SDK auto-generate one.
* Multimodal: attach images (and other media) to prompts so the model reasons over text and images together in the same conversation â€” see [Multimodal](/sdk/ai-capabilities/multimodal).
* Multi-job continuous batching: load with `modelConfig.parallel >= 2` (default `1`) to run several `completion()` calls in parallel on one loaded model. Up to `parallel` prompts finish in roughly the time of the slowest one (extras queue), and each call has its own `requestId` so you can cancel one without touching the others â€” see [Concurrent completions](#concurrent-completions).
* Batch processing: run multiple prompts through a single loaded model in one call with `batchCompletion()` â€” optimizes resources and reduces total run time. See [Batch processing](/sdk/ai-capabilities/batch-processing).
* Speculative decoding: load with `modelConfig.spec_type` to draft several tokens per step and verify them in one decode, with multi-token-prediction (MTP) layers, the model's own or an external head, or with a separate DFlash draft model. Output keeps the distribution of plain decoding. See [Speculative decoding](#speculative-decoding).

## Examples

### Usage

The canonical way to consume `completion()` is the `events` async iterable plus the aggregated `final` promise. The following script shows how to handle each event type and read the aggregated result:

<Tabs>
  <Tab value="js" label="JavaScript" default>
    <WrapCode>
      ```js file=<rootDir>/packages/sdk/dist/examples/completion-events.js title="completion-events.js" lineNumbers
      /**
       * Event-driven completion â€” demonstrates the unified `CompletionEvent` stream.
       *
       * `completion()` returns a `CompletionRun` with two primary surfaces:
       *
       *  - `events`  â€” an `AsyncIterable<CompletionEvent>` of ordered, typed events
       *                (`contentDelta`, `thinkingDelta`, `toolCall`, `toolError`,
       *                 `completionStats`, `completionDone`, `rawDelta`).
       *  - `final`   â€” a `Promise<CompletionFinal>` that resolves once the stream
       *                ends, providing aggregated `contentText`, `thinkingText`,
       *                `toolCalls`, `stats`, and `raw.fullText`.
       *
       * Set `captureThinking: true` to attempt best-effort `<think>` block parsing
       * into dedicated `thinkingDelta` events. `final.raw.fullText` keeps the exact
       * model output.
       */
      import { completion, loadModel, unloadModel, QWEN3_600M_INST_Q4 } from '@qvac/sdk';
      try {
          const modelId = await loadModel({
              modelSrc: QWEN3_600M_INST_Q4,
              modelConfig: { ctx_size: 4096 },
              onProgress: (p) => {
                  const mb = (n) => (n / 1e6).toFixed(1);
                  const line = `â–¸ Downloading ${p.percentage.toFixed(0)}% (${mb(p.downloaded)}/${mb(p.total)} MB)`;
                  process.stderr.write(process.stderr.isTTY ? `\r${line}` : `${line}\n`);
                  if (p.percentage >= 100)
                      process.stderr.write('\n');
              }
          });
          console.log(`â–¸ Model loaded: ${modelId}`);
          const result = completion({
              modelId,
              history: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Explain quantum computing in 2 sentences' }],
              stream: true,
              captureThinking: true
          });
          for await (const event of result.events) {
              handleEvent(event);
          }
          const final = await result.final;
          console.log('\nâ–¸ Final result');
          console.log(`â–¸ Content: ${final.contentText}`);
          if (final.thinkingText) {
              console.log(`â–¸ Thinking: ${final.thinkingText}`);
          }
          if (final.stats) {
              console.log(`â–¸ ${final.stats.tokensPerSecond?.toFixed(1)} tok/s`);
          }
          if (final.toolCalls.length > 0) {
              console.log(`â–¸ Tool calls: ${final.toolCalls.map((c) => c.name).join(', ')}`);
          }
          if (final.stopReason) {
              console.log(`â–¸ Stop reason: ${final.stopReason}`);
          }
          console.log(`â–¸ Raw output length: ${final.raw.fullText.length} chars`);
          await unloadModel({ modelId, clearStorage: false });
      }
      catch (error) {
          console.error('âœ–', error);
          process.exit(1);
      }
      function handleEvent(event) {
          switch (event.type) {
              case 'contentDelta':
                  process.stdout.write(event.text);
                  break;
              case 'thinkingDelta':
                  process.stdout.write(`\x1b[2m${event.text}\x1b[0m`);
                  break;
              case 'toolCall':
                  console.log(`\nâ–¸ Tool: ${event.call.name}(${JSON.stringify(event.call.arguments)})`);
                  break;
              case 'toolError':
                  console.log(`\nâœ– Tool error [${event.error.code}]: ${event.error.message}`);
                  break;
              case 'completionStats':
                  console.log(`\nâ–¸ ${event.stats.tokensPerSecond?.toFixed(1)} tok/s`);
                  break;
              case 'completionDone':
                  if (event.stopReason === 'error' && 'error' in event) {
                      console.log(`\nâœ– ${event.error.message}`);
                  }
                  break;
              case 'rawDelta':
                  break;
          }
      }
      ```
    </WrapCode>
  </Tab>
