# HTTP server (/cli/http-server)



## Overview

To run the server, install the `@qvac/cli` npm package â€” it depends on `@qvac/sdk` directly, so the SDK is installed automatically. The server is provided by `@qvac/cli` and internally translates HTTP requests into SDK calls.

## Surfaces

`qvac serve` runs the QVAC API. Additional surfaces are extensions, mounted by
their own flag:

| Surface           | Mounted with | Paths        |
| ----------------- | ------------ | ------------ |
| QVAC              | `qvac serve` | `/qvac/v1/*` |
| OpenAI-compatible | `--openai`   | `/v1/*`      |

```bash
qvac serve --openai
```

Any system compatible with the [OpenAI REST API](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview) can then point to `http://localhost:11434/v1/` and work without changes.

Pass `--no-default` to leave the QVAC surface out. Introspection
(`/openapi.json`, and `/docs` with `--docs`) is always served and describes
exactly what you mounted.

<Callout type="warn">
  `qvac serve openai` is deprecated; it is equivalent to `qvac serve --openai --no-default`.
</Callout>

## AI capabilities

At the moment, the OpenAI-compatible extension supports the following QVAC AI capabilities:

* Text generation â€” via [Chat](#chat) (`/v1/chat/completions`), [Responses](#responses) (`/v1/responses`, modern), or [Legacy completions](#legacy-completions) (`/v1/completions`).
* [Text embeddings](#embeddings) â€” via `/v1/embeddings`.
* [Decisions](#decisions) via `/v1/decisions`, for predicate, choice, and score questions about text.
* RAG â€” via [Files](#files) (`/v1/files`) and [Vector stores](#vector-stores) (`/v1/vector_stores`).
* [Image generation](#images) â€” via `/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits`.
* [Video generation](#videos) â€” via `/v1/videos`.
* Transcription â€” via [Audio](#audio) (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`).
* Text-to-speech â€” via [Audio](#audio) (`/v1/audio/speech`).
* Translation (audio-to-English only) â€” via [Audio](#audio) (`/v1/audio/translations`, Whisper translate task).

The QVAC surface supports:

* [Batch chat completion](#post-qvacv1chatbatch) â€” via `/qvac/v1/chat/batch`, several prompts decoded together on one LLM.
* [System resources](#get-qvacv1system) â€” via `/qvac/v1/system`: the host's CPU, memory and GPUs.
* [Model fit](#post-qvacv1modelsfit) â€” via `/qvac/v1/models/fit`: whether models are likely to fit, before loading them.
* [Text translation](#post-qvacv1translate) â€” via `/qvac/v1/translate`, backed by an NMT model.
* [OCR](#post-qvacv1ocr) â€” via `/qvac/v1/ocr`, text recognition in an image.
* [Image classification](#post-qvacv1classifications) â€” via `/qvac/v1/classifications`, ranked labels for an image.
* [Model registry](#get-qvacv1registrymodels) â€” via `/qvac/v1/registry/models`: browse and search the live registry, read-only.
* [Image upscaling](#post-qvacv1imagesupscale) â€” via `/qvac/v1/images/upscale`, backed by an ESRGAN model.
* [Music](#music-qvacv1audio) â€” via `/qvac/v1/audio/generations`, `/qvac/v1/audio/edits` and `/qvac/v1/audio/understandings`, backed by an `audiogen` model.

## Running the server

<Steps>
  <Step>
    Install the CLI globally (this also installs `@qvac/sdk` as a transitive dependency):

    ```bash
    npm install -g @qvac/cli
    ```

    See [System requirements](/sdk/system-requirements#environment-setup) for environment-specific instructions (e.g., Linux Vulkan runtime, Windows GPU drivers).
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Create the `qvac.config.json` file at the root of your project declaring which models the server can load. The recommended way is to let the CLI assemble it for you:

    ```bash
    qvac configure           # interactive: pick models by capability or search
    qvac configure --yes     # non-interactive: chat + transcription starter
    ```

    `qvac configure` searches the SDK's model catalog, previews the exact `serve.models` entry it will write, and merges into an existing `qvac.config.json` â€” see [`qvac configure`](/cli#qvac-configure) for the full reference.

    <Callout type="info">
      **Prefer to write it by hand?** Any of `qvac.config.{json,js,mjs,ts}` works. `qvac configure` only writes JSON; skip it and author the file yourself if you want a `.js` or `.ts` config, or if you need to set fields beyond `serve.models` (such as `plugins`, `cacheDirectory`, or `serve.cors`) at the same time. See [Configuration â€” `ServeConfig`](/sdk/configuration#serveconfig) for the full schema. Minimal example:

      ```json title="qvac.config.json"
      {
        "serve": {
          "models": {
            "my-llm": {
              "model": "QWEN3_600M_INST_Q4",
              "default": true,
              "config": { "ctx_size": 8192 }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      ```
    </Callout>
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Start the server:

    ```bash
    qvac serve --openai
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Send a request:

    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "model": "my-llm",
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
      }'
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Configuration

Models are declared in `qvac.config.*` under the `serve.models` key. The server can only load models listed under this key â€” requests for unlisted models return 404. Each key in `serve.models` is a **model alias** â€” the name that HTTP clients use in the `model` field of their requests. For the full schema of `serve.models`, see [Configuration â€” `ServeConfig`](/sdk/configuration#serveconfig).

<Card href="/cli/http-server/connection" title="Connect AI tools">
  Learn how to use the HTTP server as a local model provider for AI tools that support OpenAI-compatible API.
</Card>

### Example

```json title="qvac.config.json"
{
  "serve": {
    "models": {
      "my-llm": {
        "model": "QWEN3_600M_INST_Q4",
        "default": true,
        "preload": true,
        "config": { "ctx_size": 8192, "tools": true }
      },
      "my-embed": {
        "model": "GTE_LARGE_FP16",
        "default": true
      },
      "whisper": {
        "model": "WHISPER_TINY",
        "default": true,
        "preload": true,
        "config": { "language": "en", "strategy": "greedy" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

* **`model`**: SDK model constant name (e.g., `QWEN3_600M_INST_Q4`). The server resolves it to a download source and addon type automatically.
* **`default`**: when `true`, marks this model as the default for its endpoint category. This does not make the server auto-select the model for requests that omit `model`.
* **`preload`**: when `true`, the model is loaded into memory on server startup. When `false`, it is loaded lazily on the first request that names it (cold start â€” that request blocks while the model loads; concurrent first requests share a single load). Defaults to `true` for constant model entries and `false` for explicit `{ src, type }` entries. Use `--model <alias>` to force a lazy model to warm at startup.
* **`modelFitPolicy`**: what the engine fitter's verdict does to this alias's load: `log`, `refuse`, or `off`. Overrides the engine-level `modelFitPolicy` for this alias only. See [`modelFitPolicy`](/sdk/models/assess-model-fit#modelfitpolicy).
* **`config`**: model config overrides passed to the underlying addon. Same options as [`modelConfig` in `loadModel()`](/sdk/reference/api#loadmodel).

Lazy-load behavior (whether requests may load models on demand, load concurrency, per-load timeout, and cancel-on-disconnect) is tuned under [`serve.load`](/sdk/configuration#loadoptions-serveload), with matching `qvac serve --openai` flags. Set `serve.load.lazy: false` (or `--no-lazy-load`) to require preloaded models and return `503 model_not_loaded` otherwise.

<Callout type="info">
  The default LLM context window is 1,024 tokens and includes both the input and generated output. Set `config.ctx_size` explicitly for longer prompts. A request's `max_tokens` limits only generated tokens, so budget the prompt and requested output together within `ctx_size`.
</Callout>

<Callout type="warn">
  `default` field **does not** act as a fallback when an API request omits `model`. Requests must still include a `model` field; otherwise, the server returns `400`.
</Callout>

### Endpoint categories

Each alias gets an endpoint category from its model type, and a route only accepts aliases of its own category (`400 invalid_model_type` otherwise). The [model catalog](#model-catalog-browse) reports it as `role`.

| Model type                                                                                     | Category            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `llamacpp-completion`, `llm`                                                                   | `chat`              |
| `llamacpp-embedding`, `embeddings`                                                             | `embedding`         |
| `llamacpp-decision`                                                                            | `decision`          |
| `whispercpp-transcription`, `parakeet-transcription`, `moss-transcribe`, `whisper`, `parakeet` | `transcription`     |
| `whispercpp-audio-translation`                                                                 | `audio-translation` |
| `bci-whispercpp-transcription`, `bci`                                                          | `bci`               |
| `nmtcpp-translation`, `nmt`                                                                    | `translation`       |
| `tts-ggml`, `onnx-tts`, `tts`                                                                  | `speech`            |
| `ggml-ocr`, `ocr`                                                                              | `ocr`               |
| `ggml-classification`, `classification`                                                        | `classification`    |
| `audiogen-ggml`, `audiogen`                                                                    | `audiogen`          |
| `ggml-vla`, `vla`                                                                              | `vla`               |
| `sdcpp-generation`, `diffusion`                                                                | by `config.mode`    |
| `sdcpp-video`                                                                                  | `video`             |

An `sdcpp-generation` model serves one operation, chosen by `config.mode`: `diffusion` (the default) is `image`, and `video`, `upscale` and `world` are categories of the same name. Any other `mode` fails at startup.

```json title="qvac.config.json"
{
  "serve": {
    "models": {
      "upscaler": { "model": "REALESRGAN_X4PLUS", "config": { "mode": "upscale" } }
    }
  }
}
```

## Integration

To create a client, you can use any OpenAI-compatible AI SDK provider, such as [Vercel AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev). For a better developer experience, use our npm package `@qvac/ai-sdk-provider`.

<Card href="/cli/http-server/integration" title="Use @qvac/ai-sdk-provider">
  Vercel AI SDK provider for QVAC: introspection of supported models, automatic configuration, branded export, and more.
</Card>

## CLI

Relevant options are summarized below; run `qvac serve --help` for the exact generated help output.

| Option                    | Summary                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--openai`                | Mount the OpenAI-compatible surface                                                             |
| `--no-default`            | Do not mount the QVAC surface                                                                   |
| `-c, --config <path>`     | Config file path (default: auto-detect `qvac.config.*`)                                         |
| `-p, --port <number>`     | Port to listen on (default: `11434`)                                                            |
| `-H, --host <address>`    | Host to bind to (default: `127.0.0.1`)                                                          |
| `--model <alias>`         | Model alias to preload (repeatable; must be in config)                                          |
| `--api-key <key>`         | Require Bearer token authentication                                                             |
| `--api-key-file <path>`   | Read the Bearer token from a file instead of argv                                               |
| `--allow-unauthenticated` | Permit binding to a non-loopback host without a key                                             |
| `--cors`                  | Validate that an explicit trusted origin is configured                                          |
| `--cors-origin <origin>`  | Add a trusted CORS origin (repeatable; no wildcard)                                             |
| `--allowed-host <host>`   | Accept this `Host` header besides loopback, IP addresses and the bind host (repeatable)         |
| `--allow-any-host`        | Accept any `Host` header (turns off DNS-rebinding protection)                                   |
| `--public-base-url <url>` | Externally reachable origin required for image `response_format=url`                            |
| `--docs`                  | Mount Swagger UI at `/docs` and add same-port loopback CORS origins (requires a fixed `--port`) |
| `--ready-fd <fd>`         | Write `QVAC_SERVE_READY {"port":â€¦,"pid":â€¦}` to this inherited descriptor once listening         |
| `-v, --verbose`           | Detailed output                                                                                 |

### CORS

CORS is disabled unless trusted origins are supplied through repeatable `--cors-origin` flags or `serve.cors.origins` in `qvac.config.*`, or `--docs` adds its same-port loopback defaults. Origins must be exact HTTP(S) origins without credentials, paths, queries, or fragments. Wildcard (`*`) access is not supported.

```bash
qvac serve --openai \
  --cors-origin https://app.example.com \
  --cors-origin http://localhost:3000
```

The legacy `--cors` flag is retained as a compatibility validation switch, but it does not enable CORS by itself. It requires at least one explicit origin from `--cors-origin` or `serve.cors.origins`; otherwise startup fails. `--cors --docs` also fails without an explicit origin because the docs defaults are added only after this validation. Existing scripts can migrate as follows:

```bash
# Before
qvac serve --openai --cors

# After
qvac serve --openai --cors --cors-origin https://app.example.com
```

### Host header

CORS only governs cross-origin requests. A page that points its own domain at `127.0.0.1` (DNS rebinding) is same-origin with the server, so the server also checks the `Host` header. Requests are served only when it names a loopback host (`localhost`, `*.localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `[::1]`), an IP address, the bind host, the `--public-base-url` host or an allowed host; the port is ignored. Anything else, `/openapi.json` included, gets `403 host_not_allowed`.

Add names that reach the server through a proxy or DNS with `--allowed-host` or `serve.allowedHosts`. A leading dot covers the domain and its subdomains:

```bash
qvac serve --openai --allowed-host qvac.internal --allowed-host .corp.example
```

`--allow-any-host` (or `"allowedHosts": true`) turns the check off.

## QVAC API

Served by the QVAC surface, mounted by default. Base path: `/qvac/v1`.

### Binary inputs

Routes that take an image or other file accept it in any of three forms, under the field name the route documents:

* a `multipart/form-data` file part;
* a base64 data URL, `data:<type>;base64,...`, as a JSON string or a multipart text part;
* the `id` of a file uploaded with [`POST /v1/files`](#files), which needs the OpenAI surface mounted.

Uploads are capped at 100 MB per file and 10 files per request.

| HTTP | `error.code`       | When                                                         |
| ---- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 400  | `invalid_data_url` | Data URL is not base64-encoded, or its payload is not base64 |
| 400  | `file_not_found`   | Value is neither a data URL nor the id of an uploaded file   |
| 400  | `empty_input`      | The input has no bytes                                       |

### KV cache

Chat requests cache each conversation's prefix under `~/.qvac/kv-cache`, so a follow-up turn only prefills the new tail. Chat is the only endpoint that caches â€” Responses and Legacy completions run uncached and leave nothing here to reclaim. The directory grows on the order of hundreds of megabytes per conversation, but it is **bounded** â€” you do not need to write a sweeper of your own.

| Bound           | Value                                                 |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Size quota      | 4 GiB least-recently-used (512 MiB on mobile)         |
| Idle TTL        | 24 hours                                              |
| Sweep frequency | After a cached turn finishes, at most every 5 minutes |

Caches held by an in-flight request are never evicted.

<Callout type="warn">
  **Named caches are not covered.** The policy applies only to the *automatic* caches these endpoints create. A caller-owned named cache â€” `completion({ kvCache: "my-session" })` through the SDK â€” is exempt from both the quota and the TTL, and the endpoint below never touches it. Clean those up with [`deleteCache({ kvCacheKey })`](/sdk/reference/api#deletecache). The server itself only ever creates automatic caches; it does not use named keys.
</Callout>

### `DELETE /qvac/v1/kv_cache`

Frees every automatic KV cache no in-flight request is using, immediately, rather than waiting for the quota or the TTL. Use it when reclaiming disk matters more than keeping conversations warm: deleting a cache costs the next turn a full prefill instead of a partial one, and loses no conversation content, since a KV cache is derived data.

```bash
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/kv_cache
```

Response:

```json
{ "object": "kv_cache.reclaim", "deleted": true }
```

A failed delete returns `500 kv_cache_reclaim_failed`.

<Callout type="info">
  **Scope is the host, not this server.** `~/.qvac/kv-cache` is shared by every QVAC process running under the same home directory, so this reclaims another local process's automatic caches too. That is the same scope the automatic sweep already acts on. Nothing in a cache path identifies the process that wrote it, because cache identity is content-derived, so per-server scoping is not available.
</Callout>

This route needs the QVAC surface mounted. It is absent under `--no-default`, and therefore under the deprecated `qvac serve openai`, which implies it.

### `POST /qvac/v1/chat/batch`

Run several chat prompts through one loaded LLM in a single request, backed by the SDK's
[`batchCompletion()`](/sdk/reference/api#batchcompletion). The model decodes them together,
which is faster than sending the same prompts one by one.

`model` names a `serve.models` alias whose endpoint category is `chat` and whose
`config.parallel` is 2 or more. Up to `parallel` prompts decode at once and the rest queue.
The slots share the alias's `ctx_size`.

| Field     | Type       | Required | Meaning                                              |
| --------- | ---------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`   | `string`   | Yes      | A `serve.models` alias with endpoint category `chat` |
| `prompts` | `object[]` | Yes      | 1 to 64 prompts                                      |

Each prompt takes these [Chat](#chat) fields: `messages` (required), `tools`, `tool_choice`,
`parallel_tool_calls`, `response_format`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `seed`,
`frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` and
`reasoning_budget`. It may also carry an `id`, unique within the batch. Tools with
`defer_loading` are not supported.

`results` comes back in prompt order. Each entry has its `id` (the one given, or one the
server assigned), `index`, an assistant `message` shaped like a Chat choice, and
`finish_reason`. `stats` covers the whole batch; the engine does not break it down per
prompt.

```json
{
  "object": "chat.batch",
  "model": "my-llm",
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "cherry",
      "index": 0,
      "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "CHERRY" },
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    },
    {
      "id": "banana",
      "index": 1,
      "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "BANANA" },
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    }
  ],
  "stats": { "tokensPerSecond": 226.7, "avgConcurrentSeq": 1.98 }
}
```

The batch succeeds or fails as a whole. The request blocks until every prompt finishes, and a
client disconnect cancels it.

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/chat/batch \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"my-llm","prompts":[
        {"id":"cherry","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with only the word CHERRY."}]},
        {"id":"banana","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with only the word BANANA."}]}
      ]}'
```

| HTTP | `error.code`                 | When                                                |
| ---- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| 400  | `invalid_json`               | Body is not valid JSON                              |
| 400  | `missing_model`              | `model` is missing                                  |
| 400  | `invalid_prompts`            | `prompts` is missing, empty or carries a bad prompt |
| 400  | `too_many_prompts`           | `prompts` carries more than 64 entries              |
| 400  | `duplicate_prompt_id`        | Two prompts share an `id`                           |
| 400  | `invalid_request`            | The body carries an unknown top-level field         |
| 400  | `batch_not_enabled`          | The alias's `config.parallel` is below 2            |
| 400  | `deferred_tools_unsupported` | A prompt's tool sets `defer_loading`                |
| 400  | `tools_not_enabled`          | A prompt has `tools` and the alias lacks `tools`    |
| 400  | `invalid_response_format`    | Bad `response_format`, or one combined with `tools` |
| 400  | `invalid_tool_choice`        | `tool_choice` names no declared tool                |
| 400  | `unsupported_image_content`  | An image is not a PNG or JPEG data URL              |
| 400  | `invalid_model_type`         | Alias is not a `chat` model                         |
| 400  | `context_length_exceeded`    | The batch does not fit the context window           |
| 404  | `model_not_found`            | Unknown alias                                       |
| 429  | `request_rejected_by_policy` | The model is busy and its policy rejects queueing   |
| 502  | `inference_failed`           | Inference failed                                    |
| 503  | `model_not_loaded`           | Model not loaded and lazy loading is disabled       |

Configure the alias with at least two `parallel` slots:

```json title="qvac.config.json"
{
  "serve": {
    "models": {
      "my-llm": {
        "model": "QWEN3_600M_INST_Q4",
        "config": { "ctx_size": 8192, "parallel": 4 }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### `GET /qvac/v1/system`

Report the capacity of the host the server runs on, backed by the SDK's `getSystemResources()`.

`capabilities` describes the CPU, total memory and each GPU with its graphics drivers.
`?sample=true` adds `sample`: CPU load, memory in use (system-wide and for the serving process),
and per-GPU utilization at the time of the request.

Every figure is a metric with a `status`. Only `supported` carries a `value`, with the
`provenance` it was read from. `unavailable`, `unverified` and `failed` mean the platform could
not give a trustworthy number, and may carry a `reason`.

```bash
curl -sS "http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/system?sample=true"
```

```json
{
  "object": "system",
  "capabilities": {
    "cpu": { "status": "supported", "value": { "logicalCores": { "status": "supported", "value": 14, "provenance": { "source": "os" } } } },
    "memory": { "totalBytes": { "status": "supported", "value": 25769803776, "provenance": { "source": "os" } } },
    "gpus": { "status": "supported", "value": [] }
  },
  "sample": { "sampledAt": 1760870400000, "cpu": { "status": "supported", "value": 0.12, "provenance": { "source": "os" } } }
}
```

The example is trimmed; each CPU, memory and GPU object carries every field, each as a metric.

| HTTP | `error.code`              | When                                    |
| ---- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| 400  | `invalid_sample`          | `sample` is not `true` or `false`       |
| 500  | `system_resources_failed` | The SDK could not read system resources |

### `POST /qvac/v1/models/fit`

Ask whether models are likely to fit in the host's memory before loading them, backed by the
SDK's `assessModelFit()`. Nothing is downloaded or loaded: each model's weightless registry
description is fetched (tens of KB) and the engine's own fitter runs against it, falling back to
a floor computed from catalog facts.

| Field                  | Type                           | Required | Meaning                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `models`               | `object[]`                     | Yes      | Up to 16 models, assessed together under one budget      |
| `models[].model`       | `string`                       | Yes      | A `serve.models` alias, or an SDK model constant name    |
| `models[].modelConfig` | `object`                       | No       | Config to assess with, merged over an alias's own config |
| `execution`            | `"sequential" \| "concurrent"` | No       | Co-residency assumption; `sequential` by default         |
| `policy`               | `"interactive-v1"`             | No       | Headroom policy; withholds 20% of available memory       |

An alias is assessed with the config it would load with. `modelConfig` is merged over it key
by key, nested objects included, so `{"ctx_size": 32768}` asks about a longer context and an
override inside `contextParams` keeps the alias's other context params. Model sources cannot be given in the request:
companion sources in `modelConfig` (`*ModelSrc` keys) must name SDK model constants, so a request
never makes the server read a path or URL of its choosing.

The answer is advisory. `verdict` is `likely-fits`, `likely-too-large` or `unknown`, combined
across every model under `execution`. `unknown` means the evidence supports neither answer, not
"no". `models` carries one verdict per entry in request order, and `budget` the memory it was
judged against.

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/models/fit \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"models":[{"model":"my-llm","modelConfig":{"ctx_size":8192}}]}'
```

```json
{
  "object": "model_fit",
  "verdict": "likely-fits",
  "basis": "system-memory",
  "execution": "sequential",
  "evidence": "native-fit",
  "budget": {
    "totalBytes": 25769803776,
    "usedBytes": 21211299840,
    "availableBytes": 4558503936,
    "reservedBytes": 911700787,
    "availableAfterReserveBytes": 3646803149
  },
  "models": [
    {
      "model": "my-llm",
      "name": "QWEN3_600M_INST_Q4",
      "verdict": "likely-fits",
      "evidence": "native-fit",
      "device": "gpu",
      "reasons": ["..."]
    }
  ],
  "reasons": ["..."],
  "assumptions": ["..."]
}
```

| HTTP | `error.code`        | When                                                       |
| ---- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| 400  | `invalid_json`      | Body is not valid JSON                                     |
| 400  | `invalid_models`    | `models` is missing or empty, or an entry is malformed     |
| 400  | `too_many_models`   | `models` carries more than 16 entries                      |
| 400  | `invalid_execution` | `execution` is not `sequential` or `concurrent`            |
| 400  | `invalid_policy`    | `policy` is not `interactive-v1`                           |
| 400  | `invalid_model_src` | A companion source in `modelConfig` is not an SDK constant |
| 400  | `invalid_request`   | The body carries an unknown field                          |
| 404  | `model_not_found`   | An entry names neither an alias nor an SDK model constant  |
| 500  | `model_fit_failed`  | The SDK assessment failed                                  |

### `POST /qvac/v1/translate`

Translate text with an NMT model, backed by the SDK's `translate()`.

`model` names a `serve.models` alias whose endpoint category is `translation`.
That alias configures the engine and the language direction, as shown at the end
of this section.

| Field    | Type                 | Required | Meaning                                                     |
| -------- | -------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`  | `string`             | Yes      | A `serve.models` alias with endpoint category `translation` |
| `text`   | `string \| string[]` | Yes      | One input, or an array of up to 100 for batch               |
| `stream` | `boolean`            | No       | Stream Server-Sent Events                                   |

`translations` comes back in the order the inputs were given, one entry per
input:

```json
{
  "object": "translation",
  "model": "ta-en",
  "translations": ["Hello, world."],
  "stats": { "totalTime": 41 }
}
```

`stats` is returned for a single input; a batch does not report stats.

Streaming a single input emits `translation.chunk` events carrying `delta` as
the text is decoded. Streaming an array emits one `translation.item` per input,
carrying `index` and the whole `text`, and these arrive together once the batch
finishes. Both end with one `translation.done` event, then `data: [DONE]`.

A client disconnect cancels the request and its result is dropped.

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/translate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"ta-en","text":"à®µà®£à®•à¯à®•à®®à¯ à®‰à®²à®•à®®à¯"}'
```

| HTTP | `error.code`         | When                                          |
| ---- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| 400  | `invalid_json`       | Body is not valid JSON                        |
| 400  | `missing_model`      | `model` is missing                            |
| 400  | `missing_text`       | `text` is missing or empty                    |
| 400  | `too_many_inputs`    | `text` carries more than 100 inputs           |
| 400  | `invalid_request`    | The body carries an unknown field             |
| 400  | `invalid_model_type` | Alias is not a `translation` model            |
| 404  | `model_not_found`    | Unknown alias                                 |
| 503  | `model_not_loaded`   | Model not loaded and lazy loading is disabled |

Configure a translation model with its engine and direction:

```json title="qvac.config.json"
{
  "serve": {
    "models": {
      "ta-en": {
        "model": "BERGAMOT_TA_EN",
        "config": { "engine": "Bergamot", "from": "ta", "to": "en" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### `POST /qvac/v1/ocr`

Read the text in an image with an OCR model, backed by the SDK's `ocr()`.

`model` names a `serve.models` alias whose endpoint category is `ocr`. That
alias configures the pipeline and the languages, as shown at the end of this
section. Send the request as JSON or `multipart/form-data`.

| Field       | Type               | Required | Meaning                                                        |
| ----------- | ------------------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`     | `string`           | Yes      | A `serve.models` alias with endpoint category `ocr`            |
| `image`     | file, data URL, id | Yes      | A PNG, JPEG or BMP, in any [binary input](#binary-inputs) form |
| `paragraph` | `boolean`          | No       | Merge nearby lines into paragraph blocks. Default `false`      |
| `stream`    | `boolean`          | No       | Stream Server-Sent Events                                      |

Multipart flags are sent as the text `true` or `false`.

`blocks` lists the recognised text in reading order. `bbox` is
`[xMin, yMin, xMax, yMax]` in image pixels; `bbox` and `confidence` are present
when the engine reports them.

```json
{
  "object": "ocr",
  "model": "ocr-en",
  "blocks": [{ "text": "Type to enter text", "bbox": [405, 393, 688, 433], "confidence": 0.98 }],
  "stats": { "detectionTime": 210, "recognitionTime": 95, "totalTime": 312 }
}
```

Streaming emits `ocr.chunk` events carrying `blocks` as the engine returns
them, then one `ocr.done` event with `stats`, then `data: [DONE]`. The engine
currently returns all of an image's blocks at once, so expect a single
`ocr.chunk`. An error before it, such as an image the engine cannot
decode, returns JSON as usual; a failure after it arrives as a final
`{ "error": ... }` event.

OCR cannot be cancelled: a client disconnect drops the result, but the image is
still read to the end.

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/ocr \
  -F model=ocr-en \
  -F image=@receipt.png
```

The [binary input](#binary-inputs) errors apply to `image`, plus:

| HTTP | `error.code`               | When                                             |
| ---- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| 400  | `invalid_json`             | Body is not valid JSON                           |
| 400  | `invalid_multipart`        | Multipart body could not be parsed               |
| 400  | `missing_model`            | `model` is missing                               |
| 400  | `missing_image`            | `image` is missing or empty                      |
| 400  | `unsupported_image_format` | `image` is not a PNG, JPEG or BMP, or is corrupt |
| 400  | `invalid_request`          | Unknown field, or a flag that is not boolean     |
| 400  | `invalid_model_type`       | Alias is not an `ocr` model                      |
| 404  | `model_not_found`          | Unknown alias                                    |
| 413  | `request_too_large`        | Upload over 100 MB                               |
| 503  | `model_not_loaded`         | Model not loaded and lazy loading is disabled    |

Configure an OCR model with its languages. The detector model is derived from
the recognizer; `OCR_DOCTR` selects the language-agnostic DocTR pipeline.

```json title="qvac.config.json"
{
  "serve": {
    "models": {
      "ocr-en": {
        "model": "OCR_LATIN",
        "config": { "langList": ["en"] }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### `POST /qvac/v1/classifications`

Classify an image with a classification model, backed by the SDK's `classify()`.

`model` names a `serve.models` alias whose endpoint category is `classification`. Send the
request as JSON or `multipart/form-data`.

| Field   | Type               | Required | Meaning                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model` | `string`           | Yes      | A `serve.models` alias with endpoint category `classification` |
| `image` | file, data URL, id | Yes      | A PNG or JPEG, in any [binary input](#binary-inputs) form      |
| `top_k` | `integer`          | No       | Return only the K most likely labels. Default: every label     |

`results` ranks the labels by `confidence`, highest first.

```json
{
  "object": "classification",
  "model": "classifier",
  "results": [
    { "label": "food", "confidence": 0.93 },
    { "label": "other", "confidence": 0.05 },
    { "label": "report", "confidence": 0.02 }
  ]
}
```

Classification cannot be cancelled: a client disconnect drops the result, but the image is
still classified.

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/classifications \
  -F model=classifier \
  -F image=@photo.jpg \
  -F top_k=1
```

The [binary input](#binary-inputs) errors apply to `image`, plus:

| HTTP | `error.code`               | When                                          |
| ---- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| 400  | `invalid_json`             | Body is not valid JSON                        |
| 400  | `invalid_multipart`        | Multipart body could not be parsed            |
| 400  | `missing_model`            | `model` is missing                            |
| 400  | `missing_image`            | `image` is missing or empty                   |
| 400  | `unsupported_image_format` | `image` is not a PNG or JPEG, or is corrupt   |
| 400  | `invalid_request`          | Unknown field, or `top_k` not a positive int  |
| 400  | `invalid_model_type`       | Alias is not a `classification` model         |
| 404  | `model_not_found`          | Unknown alias                                 |
| 413  | `request_too_large`        | Upload over 100 MB                            |
| 503  | `model_not_loaded`         | Model not loaded and lazy loading is disabled |

Configure a classification model:

```json title="qvac.config.json"
{
  "serve": {
    "models": {
      "classifier": { "type": "ggml-classification" }
    }
  }
}
```

An alias without `src` loads the addon's bundled MobileNetV3-Small, whose labels are `food`,
`report` and `other`. Set `src` to the path of a GGUF classifier to use your own; its labels
come from the GGUF metadata.

### `GET /qvac/v1/registry/models`

Browse and search the live QVAC model registry, backed by the SDK's
`modelRegistrySearch()`. Read-only: nothing is downloaded or loaded.

Filter with query params (all optional, combined with AND); with none, every
entry is listed.

| Param          | Meaning                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `search`       | Case-insensitive substring match on name, registry path, addon or engine |
| `addon`        | Addon / capability category: `llm`, `whisper`, `embeddings`, `ocr`, â€¦    |
| `engine`       | Inference engine, e.g. `llamacpp-completion`                             |
| `quantization` | e.g. `q4`                                                                |
| `limit`        | Page size; omit for no limit (returns all matching entries)              |
| `offset`       | Rows to skip (default 0)                                                 |

Entries are registry models, not `serve.models` aliases. To call one, add an
alias whose `src` is `registry://<registrySource>/<registryPath>`. The first
request after start-up connects to the registry over P2P and can take several
seconds.

```bash
curl -sS "http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/registry/models?addon=llm&search=qwen3&limit=1"
```

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "name": "Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_0",
      "registryPath": "unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF/blob/50968a4468ef4233ed78cd7c3de230dd1d61a56b/Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_0.gguf",
      "registrySource": "hf",
      "modelId": "Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_0.gguf",
      "addon": "llm",
      "engine": "llamacpp-completion",
      "quantization": "q4",
      "params": "600M",
      "expectedSize": 382156480,
      "sha256Checksum": "33bcc57074ec7b6eada5a90651ee546ec0c2b271002c22baf9f1b2dd1e8f75cb",
      "blobCoreKey": "4035e66388340ff7c1f291e7c0101855f5d0b2c7085f3ff62213573a2cd5dd17",
      "blobBlockOffset": 380426,
      "blobBlockLength": 5832,
      "blobByteOffset": 24929383097
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true
}
```

| HTTP | `error.code`            | When                                         |
| ---- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| 400  | `invalid_addon`         | `addon` is not a registry addon              |
| 400  | `invalid_limit`         | `limit` is not a positive integer            |
| 400  | `invalid_offset`        | `offset` is not a non-negative integer       |
| 502  | `registry_query_failed` | The registry could not be reached or queried |

### `GET /qvac/v1/registry/models/lookup`

Fetch one registry entry by the `registrySource` and `registryPath` a list row
carries. Same shape as a list row. Both params are required.

```bash
curl -sS -G http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/registry/models/lookup \
  --data-urlencode registrySource=hf \
  --data-urlencode registryPath=unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF/blob/50968a4468ef4233ed78cd7c3de230dd1d61a56b/Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_0.gguf
```

| HTTP | `error.code`              | When                                         |
| ---- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| 400  | `invalid_registry_source` | `registrySource` is missing or empty         |
| 400  | `invalid_registry_path`   | `registryPath` is missing or empty           |
| 404  | `model_not_found`         | No registry entry has this source and path   |
| 502  | `registry_query_failed`   | The registry could not be reached or queried |

### `POST /qvac/v1/images/upscale`

Upscale an image with an ESRGAN model, backed by the SDK's `upscale()`.

`model` names a `serve.models` alias whose endpoint category is `upscale`: an
`sdcpp-generation` model with `config.mode: "upscale"`. Send JSON or
`multipart/form-data`; `image` takes any of the [binary input](#binary-inputs) forms.

| Field     | Type         | Required | Meaning                                                                            |
| --------- | ------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`   | `string`     | Yes      | A `serve.models` alias with endpoint category `upscale`                            |
| `image`   | binary input | Yes      | The PNG or JPEG to upscale                                                         |
| `repeats` | `integer`    | No       | Passes to run, 1 to 4 (default 1); each multiplies both sides by the model's scale |

The response has the `/v1/images` shape, with one PNG:

```json
{
  "created": 1767225600,
  "output_format": "png",
  "size": "2048x2048",
  "data": [{ "b64_json": "iVBORw0KGgo..." }]
}
```

Upscaling cannot be cancelled: a client disconnect drops the result, but the
image is still upscaled to the end.

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/images/upscale \
  -F model=upscaler -F image=@photo.png -F repeats=1
```

| HTTP | `error.code`               | When                                                                                |
| ---- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 400  | `invalid_json`             | Body is not valid JSON                                                              |
| 400  | `missing_model`            | `model` is missing                                                                  |
| 400  | `missing_image`            | `image` is missing                                                                  |
| 400  | `unsupported_image_format` | `image` is not a PNG or JPEG                                                        |
| 400  | `invalid_image`            | `image` has a PNG or JPEG header but cannot be decoded                              |
| 400  | `image_too_large`          | `image`, or its upscaled output, is over the 16,384-pixel edge or pixel-count limit |
| 400  | `invalid_repeats`          | `repeats` is not an integer from 1 to 4                                             |
| 400  | `invalid_request`          | The body carries an unknown field                                                   |
| 400  | `invalid_model_type`       | Alias is not an `upscale` model                                                     |
| 404  | `model_not_found`          | Unknown alias                                                                       |
| 503  | `model_not_loaded`         | Model not loaded and lazy loading is disabled                                       |

`image` can also fail with the [binary input](#binary-inputs) codes.

Configure an upscale model with `config.mode: "upscale"`:

```json title="qvac.config.json"
{
  "serve": {
    "models": {
      "upscaler": {
        "model": "REALESRGAN_X4PLUS",
        "config": { "mode": "upscale", "upscaler": { "tile_size": 128 } }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Music: `/qvac/v1/audio/*`

Generate, edit and describe music with an `audiogen` model, backed by the SDK's `audioGen()`,
`audioEdit()` and `audioUnderstand()`. Request fields mirror those functions' arguments, with
`model` naming the alias and each audio input in any [binary input](#binary-inputs) form.
Editing and understanding need an ACE-Step model.

Generations and edits run as async jobs, like `/v1/videos`: `POST` returns the job at once with
`status: queued`, and the client polls it, then fetches the audio. Understanding answers in one
response.

Send JSON or `multipart/form-data`. In a multipart body, numbers and flags are text parts
(`seed=42`, `simpleMode=true`), and `operations` and `audioCodes` are JSON text. Audio inputs take
any format the SDK audio decoder reads (WAV, MP3, FLAC, ...); give the upload a file name or
declare its type so the decoder can pick it.

Ranges and combinations (a `cover-nofsq` task needs `sourceAudio`, `duration` excludes
`maxFrames`, ...) are checked by the SDK and come back as `400 invalid_request` naming the rule.

#### `POST /qvac/v1/audio/generations`

| Field                                | Type               | Required | Meaning                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`                              | `string`           | Yes      | A `serve.models` alias with endpoint category `audiogen`    |
| `caption`                            | `string`           | Yes      | What to generate                                            |
| `lyrics`                             | `string`           | No       | Lyrics, or `[Instrumental]`                                 |
| `duration`                           | `number`           | No       | Approximate length in seconds                               |
| `seed`                               | `integer`          | No       | RNG seed; the seed used is in `stats.metadata.seed`         |
| `taskType`                           | `string`           | No       | `text2music` (default), `cover-nofsq` or `lego`             |
| `sourceAudio`                        | file, data URL, id | No       | Recording to re-render, for `cover-nofsq` and `lego`        |
| `referenceAudio`                     | file, data URL, id | No       | Timbre reference                                            |
| `audioCodes`                         | `integer[]`        | No       | Semantic codes to synthesize, e.g. from an understanding    |
| `simpleMode`, `rewriteQuery`         | `boolean`          | No       | Let the LM write or rewrite the request                     |
| `generateLrc`, `computeQualityScore` | `boolean`          | No       | Add `stats.lrc` / `stats.lyricsScore`, `stats.qualityScore` |

The other `audioGen()` fields (`bpm`, `keyscale`, `timesignature`, `vocalLanguage`, `track`,
`maxFrames`, `inferenceSteps`, `shift`, `cfgScale`, the `lm*` and `dcw*` controls, ...) are
accepted under the same names.

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/audio/generations \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "model": "music", "caption": "calm lofi piano", "lyrics": "[Instrumental]", "duration": 30 }'
```

```json
{
  "id": "audiogen_6f1c...",
  "object": "audio.generation",
  "model": "music",
  "status": "queued",
  "progress": 0,
  "stage": null,
  "created_at": 1761500000,
  "completed_at": null,
  "error": null,
  "stats": null
}
```

#### `POST /qvac/v1/audio/edits`

Runs an ordered pipeline of `flow-edit` and `repaint` operations over `sourceAudio`.

| Field            | Type               | Required | Meaning                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`          | `string`           | Yes      | An ACE-Step `audiogen` alias                                                        |
| `sourceAudio`    | file, data URL, id | Yes      | The recording to edit                                                               |
| `operations`     | `object[]`         | Yes      | `flow-edit` (`from`, `to` prompts) or `repaint` (`caption`, `start`, `end` seconds) |
| `referenceAudio` | file, data URL, id | No       | Timbre reference for every operation                                                |
| `seed`           | `integer`          | No       | Seeds the first operation; each next one uses `seed + index`                        |

`bpm`, `keyscale`, `timesignature`, `vocalLanguage`, `inferenceSteps`, `shift` and the `dcw*`
controls apply to every operation.

Known limitation: the SDK decodes an encoded source to mono, and a loud stereo source can mix
above full scale; the job then fails with `audio_edit_failed` (`sourceAudio must contain samples
in [-1, 1]`). Lowering the source's gain avoids it.

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:11434/qvac/v1/audio/edits \
  -F model=music \
  -F sourceAudio=@song.wav \
  -F 'operations=[{"type":"repaint","caption":"analog synth solo","start":10,"end":20}]'
```

#### Jobs

The same routes serve both job kinds, under `/qvac/v1/audio/generations` and
`/qvac/v1/audio/edits`:

| Method   | Path            | Returns                                         |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `GET`    | `/`             | Jobs, newest first; `limit`, `order`, `after`   |
| `GET`    | `/{id}`         | The job                                         |
| `GET`    | `/{id}/content` | The audio                                       |
| `DELETE` | `/{id}`         | Deletes the job, cancelling it if still running |

`status` moves `queued` â†’ `in_progress` â†’ `completed` or `failed`. `progress` (0â€“100) is the
progress of the engine stage named in `stage`, and restarts at each stage (an ACE-Step generation
runs `lm`, then the longer DiT and VAE stages); it reads 100 once the job completes. Once completed,
`stats` carries the SDK's run stats; for ACE-Step that includes `metadata`, what was rendered
after the LM filled in unset fields, and `lrc`, `lyricsScore` and `qualityScore` when requested.
A failed job carries `error.code` `audio_generation_failed` or `audio_edit_failed`.

`/content` returns 16-bit PCM WAV at the engine's rate (48 kHz stereo for ACE-Step).
`?format=mp3|flac|opus|aac` encodes it with the system `ffmpeg`.

The job store is in memory: ids and audio are lost on restart, at most 256 jobs of each kind are
kept, and the audio expires with the server's file store (1 hour).

#### `POST /qvac/v1/audio/understandings`

Describes a recording: a caption, BPM, key, time signature, language and the recovered semantic
codes, which a generation takes back as `audioCodes`. A client disconnect cancels it.

| Field                               | Type               | Required | Meaning                         |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------- |
| `model`                             | `string`           | Yes      | An ACE-Step `audiogen` alias    |
| `sourceAudio`                       | file, data URL, id | Yes      | The recording to describe       |
| `seed`                              | `integer`          | No       | Seeds the LM decode             |
| `vocalLanguage`                     | `string`           | No       | Language forced into the result |
| `lmTemperature`, `lmTopP`, `lmTopK` | `number`           | No       | LM sampling                     |

```json
{
  "object": "audio.understanding",
  "model": "music",
  "description": {
    "caption": "A calm lo-fi piano piece with soft keys.",
    "bpm": 72,
    "duration": 30,
    "keyscale": "A minor",
    "timesignature": "4/4",
    "vocalLanguage": "unknown",
    "audioCodes": [8123, 1022, 517],
    "seed": 1
  },
  "stats": { "totalTimeMs": 5200 }
}
```

#### Errors

The [binary input](#binary-inputs) errors apply to `sourceAudio` and `referenceAudio`, plus:

| HTTP | `error.code`                 | When                                                        |
| ---- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| 400  | `invalid_json`               | Body is not valid JSON                                      |
| 400  | `invalid_multipart`          | Multipart body could not be parsed                          |
| 400  | `missing_model`              | `model` is missing                                          |
| 400  | `missing_caption`            | Generation without a `caption`                              |
| 400  | `missing_source_audio`       | Edit or understanding without `sourceAudio`                 |
| 400  | `invalid_operations`         | `operations` is missing, empty or malformed                 |
| 400  | `invalid_request`            | Unknown field, wrong type, or a combination the SDK refuses |
| 400  | `invalid_model_type`         | Alias is not an `audiogen` model                            |
| 404  | `model_not_found`            | Unknown alias                                               |
| 404  | `audio_job_not_found`        | No job with that id                                         |
| 409  | `audio_job_not_ready`        | `/content` before the job completed; see `Retry-After`      |
| 409  | `audio_job_failed`           | `/content` of a failed job                                  |
| 410  | `audio_expired`              | The audio has left the file store                           |
| 413  | `request_too_large`          | Upload over 100 MB                                          |
| 502  | `audio_understanding_failed` | The engine failed to describe the recording                 |
| 502  | `transcode_failed`           | ffmpeg failed; `format=wav` still works                     |
| 503  | `transcode_unavailable`      | An encoded `format` without ffmpeg on PATH                  |
| 503  | `model_not_loaded`           | Model not loaded and lazy loading is disabled               |

#### Configuring a music model

ACE-Step takes four weights. The alias's `model` is its DiT; `config` names all four:

```json title="qvac.config.json"
{
  "serve": {
    "models": {
      "music": {
        "model": "AUDIOGEN_ACESTEP_V15_TURBO_Q4_K_M",
        "config": {
          "textEncModelSrc": "AUDIOGEN_QWEN3_EMBEDDING_0_6B_Q8_0",
          "lmModelSrc": "AUDIOGEN_ACESTEP_5HZ_LM_0_6B_Q8_0",
          "ditModelSrc": "AUDIOGEN_ACESTEP_V15_TURBO_Q4_K_M",
          "vaeModelSrc": "AUDIOGEN_VAE_BF16",
          "useGPU": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

MiniMax-Music3 sets `"engine": "minimax"` with `lmModelSrc` and `synthModelSrc`, and serves
generations only.

## OpenAI-compatible API

Served by the `--openai` extension. All endpoints follow the [OpenAI API](https://ecosystem.openai.com/docs/api-reference) request and response format. Base path: `/v1`.

### Endpoints
